title: The regulatory map
oneLiner: The Insurance Authority licenses intermediaries and supervises insurers under one Ordinance, with the HKMA supervising banks alongside.
keyPoints: **One Ordinance, one regulator:** The [[Insurance Authority]] (IA) regulates and supervises the industry under the Insurance Ordinance (Cap. 41). Its principal function is the stability of the industry and the protection of policy holders (s.4A(1)).

**Two regulated populations:** The Ordinance covers [[authorized insurers|authorized insurer]] (Part II onwards) and intermediaries. Part X licenses intermediaries and Part XI governs their conduct and discipline.

**The core prohibition:** s.64G bars anyone from carrying on a [[regulated activity]] in the course of business or for reward unless an exception in s.64G(3) applies. Breach is a criminal offence (s.64G(4)).

**The bank's supervisor:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the [[Monetary Authority]], a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases). The IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)), and it must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)).

**Layers of rules:** Section 94 rules bind intermediaries. Codes under s.95 are guidance, and a breach can count against a [[fit and proper]] assessment (s.95(6)). Guidelines under s.133 are guidance that a court must take into account where relevant (s.133(5)).
**Money and reform:** A levy is payable on premiums to fund the regulator (Cap. 41J). The risk-based capital regime began on 1 July 2024, and further reforms are pending.

points: **Statute:** The Insurance Ordinance (Cap. 41) is the current name of the Ordinance. The IA was established on 7 December 2015 under the Insurance Companies (Amendment) Ordinance 2015, and took over regulation from the Office of the Commissioner of Insurance on 26 June 2017. Confirm the renaming instrument and date on e-Legislation before citing them.
**Body corporate:** s.4AAA(1) establishes the IA as a body corporate named Insurance Authority. It has perpetual succession and can sue and be sued (s.4AAA(3)).
**Functions:** s.4A(2)(a) makes the IA responsible for supervising authorized insurers and licensed intermediaries. s.4A(2)(ea) requires it to regulate intermediaries through a licensing regime.
**Powers:** s.4B(1) lets the IA do anything necessary or incidental to its functions. Section 4B(2)(f) allows it to publish materials on any matter relating to its functions.

**Predecessor regime:** Before 23 September 2019, intermediaries were registered with three self-regulatory organizations. On that date the IA became the sole regulator of more than 100,000 intermediaries (reported).
deepDive.takeaway: Read Part IA and Part X first: together they set out who the regulator is and what it licenses.

points: **Insurers:** Authorized under Part II and supervised under Parts III to VA. Group supervision of designated holding companies sits in Part XIA.

**Five licence types:** Part X provides for a licensed insurance agency (s.64U), a licensed individual insurance agent (s.64W), a licensed technical representative (agent) (s.64Y), a licensed insurance broker company (s.64ZA) and a licensed technical representative (broker) (s.64ZC).

**Agent or broker:** An agency acts as an agent of an authorized insurer (s.64G(3)(a)). A broker company acts as agent of the policy holder for the activities in Sch. 1A, Pt 1, s.1(a) and (s.64G(3)(d)).

**Regulated activities:** Sch. 1A, Pt 1 lists negotiating or arranging a contract, inviting or inducing a person to enter a contract, inviting or inducing a material decision, and giving regulated advice (s.3A).
**Fitness and properness:** The IA must weigh qualifications, competence, reputation, financial status and any disciplinary history when licensing (s.64ZZA(1)).
deepDive.takeaway: The licence route decides which obligations apply, so settle the bank's model before anything else.

deepDive.heading: Where the bank meets the other regulators
deepDive.lede: A bank answers to the HKMA and the IA at once, and other regulators also touch insurance sales.
points: **HKMA by delegation:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases). The IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The delegated powers are those in ss.64ZZF(6) and 64ZZH(1).

**Consultation:** The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating a matter involving an authorized institution (s.64ZZH(2)). It must also consult before disciplinary action against one under s.81 (ss.82(4), 84(4)).

**Customer information:** s.64ZZJ restricts what inspectors and investigators can require from an authorized institution about customers. The limits do not apply to the Monetary Authority or a specified authority.
**SFC:** The SFC's role over investment-linked products sold by banks needs checking. See stage 2 and stage 4.
**PCPD and MPFA:** Direct marketing is governed by the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (Cap. 486), covered in stage 9. The MPFA oversees MPF intermediaries, which is outside this volume.
deepDive.takeaway: Expect shared oversight, so keep one set of records that serves the HKMA and the IA alike.

deepDive.heading: Layers of rules and their legal force
deepDive.lede: Not every rule binds in the same way, and the layers run from statute down to informal practice.

visual.caption: Legal force falls as you move down, but supervisory weight is not the same as legal force.

items.note: Binding; breach of s.64G can be an offence

items.note: Binding conduct requirements on intermediaries

points: **Ordinance:** The strongest layer. Carrying on a regulated activity without a licence attracts fines and imprisonment on conviction (s.64G(4)).
**Rules under s.94:** The IA may make rules requiring intermediaries to comply with conduct standards, including advertising controls (s.94(1), (2)(a)).
**Codes under s.95:** Non-compliance does not by itself create liability, but it may count in a fit and proper assessment (s.95(5), (6)). A code is admissible in court (s.95(7)).
**Guidelines under s.133:** Similar effect. A breach does not by itself create liability, but the court must take compliance into account where a provision is relevant (s.133(4), (5)).
**Circulars and FAQs:** These state the regulator's view. They have no statutory force of their own, and their status changes, so check each one.
deepDive.takeaway: A guideline binds no one directly, but a court must take its relevant provisions into account, so treat it as the IA's stated standard.

deepDive.heading: Levies and the regulator's funding
deepDive.lede: A levy on premiums helps fund the regulator, and a formula in subsidiary legislation sets its amount.

points: **Liability:** A levy is payable for each premium payment on specified general and long term business (Cap. 41J, s.4). Reinsurance and captive-underwritten contracts are excluded (s.4(b)).
**Premium base:** The premium is taken after discounts and refunds but before reinsurance premiums ceded and commission (s.3(1)).
**Amount:** The levy is the premium multiplied by the rate for the period in which the policy year begins (s.5). Maxima apply to scheduled premium payments in a policy year (s.6).
**Current rate:** The rate is 0.1% from 1 April 2021, with maxima of $5,000 for general and $100 for long term business (Schedule).

**Collection:** Cap. 41 s.134(1) makes the levy payable to the Authority by the policy holder, and s.134(3) lets the Authority recover it as a civil debt. The Order, Cap. 41J, sets the amount. Under Cap. 41I s.3(2), an intermediary that collects a levy for the insurer must forward it to the insurer as soon as practicable. An insurer may not keep any excess (s.3(3)). Penalties of up to $5,000 for a policy holder who does not pay, and up to $10,000 for an insurer that keeps an excess, apply under s.3(4) and (5).
deepDive.takeaway: The levy is a pricing line, not a bank fee: check its base and rate in the pricing model before launch.

deepDive.heading: Reform watch
deepDive.lede: Several reforms are live, and their status changes quickly, so check each one on the day you rely on it.
points: **Insurance (Amendment) Ordinance 2023:** Enacted on 6 July 2023 and gazetted on 14 July 2023. It brought in a designated insurance holding company concept and the risk-based capital (RBC) regime, which began on 1 July 2024.

**RBC enhancements:** The IA consulted on amending the Insurance (Valuation and Capital) Rules (Cap. 41R). It published its conclusions on 8 May 2026 and targets implementation by 31 December 2026 (proposal, check status).

**Policyholders' Protection Scheme:** Consultation ran from 30 December 2022 to 31 March 2023, and conclusions were published on 28 December 2023 announcing drafting of amendments. Check the current enactment status.
**Calendar:** Keep a reform calendar and record which version of each rule the bank relied on at each date.
deepDive.takeaway: Most of these reforms fall on insurers, but they change the terms the bank receives from its partner, so track them.

provisions.title: Functions of Authority
provisions.summary: Sets the IA's principal function of regulating and supervising the insurance industry for stability and policy holder protection. It makes the IA responsible for supervising authorized insurers and licensed intermediaries, and requires a licensing regime for intermediaries.
provisions.counselNote: This is the starting point for why the IA can license and discipline the bank's intermediary business. Cite it when explaining the IA's mandate to business teams.

provisions.title: Delegation of certain powers of Authority to Monetary Authority
provisions.summary: Allows the IA, with Chief Executive in Council approval, to delegate its inspection and investigation powers (ss.64ZZF(6), 64ZZH(1)) to the Monetary Authority for regulated activities carried on by an authorized institution. Subsection (8) adapts the references to the Monetary Authority.
provisions.counselNote: This is the legal basis for the HKMA examining a bank's insurance intermediary business. Ask the HKMA which delegation conditions apply to your bank.

provisions.title: Interpretation of Part X
provisions.summary: Defines the five licence types in Part X by reference to their grant sections (ss.64U, 64W, 64Y, 64ZA, 64ZC) and defines the agency agreement, controller and business record. The licence types are the core intermediary categories.
provisions.counselNote: Use these definitions to decide which licence the bank or its partner needs. Map each proposed sales role to one of the five types before drafting the distribution agreement.

provisions.title: Regulated Activity, Material Decision and Regulated Advice
provisions.summary: Lists the regulated activities: negotiating or arranging a contract, inviting or inducing entry into a contract, inviting or inducing a material decision, and giving regulated advice. Part 2 lists material decisions, and Part 3 covers regulated advice.
provisions.counselNote: Each app feature that presents, recommends or arranges cover may be a regulated activity. Run every product journey through this list before launch.

provisions.title: Restrictions on carrying on regulated activities
provisions.summary: Bars a person from carrying on a regulated activity in the course of business or for reward, subject to the exceptions in subsection (3). Subsection (4) makes a breach without reasonable excuse an offence, with a fine of $1,000,000 and two years' imprisonment on indictment.
provisions.counselNote: The bank must be licensed, act through a licensed agency or broker, or fall within an exception. Treat this as the gateway question for every distribution model.

provisions.title: Contracts of insurance made through persons other than licensed insurance intermediaries, etc.
provisions.summary: An authorized insurer must not enter into a contract through, or accept a referral from, a person in Hong Kong unless that person is a licensed agency or agent appointed by the insurer, a licensed broker company, or has only clerical or administrative duties. A non-compliant contract is enforceable by, or voidable at the option of, the policy holder.
provisions.counselNote: This section binds the insurer, not the bank. A referral arrangement with the bank can put the insurer in breach even where the bank never advises, so check every referral fee and lead-sharing term against this test.

provisions.title: Determination of fit and proper
provisions.summary: Sets the matters the IA must have regard to in deciding whether a person is fit and proper. They include qualifications, competence, honesty and fairness, reputation and integrity, financial status, group information, other businesses, and disciplinary action by the Monetary Authority, the SFC, the MPFA or any similar overseas body. For licence applications, it also covers persons employed or acting for the applicant and internal controls.
provisions.counselNote: Expect the IA to look at the bank's group, its officers and any HKMA or SFC history. Prepare a fit and proper pack for the bank's licence applicants.

provisions.title: Codes of conduct for licensed insurance intermediaries
provisions.summary: Lets the IA publish codes of conduct giving guidance on the practices and standards licensed intermediaries are expected to follow. A breach does not by itself create liability, but it can be taken into account in a fit and proper assessment, and the code is admissible in court.
provisions.counselNote: Treat each code as the IA's expected standard. Build the codes into the app's compliance checklist, not just the legal file.

provisions.title: Codes or guidelines on functions of Authority, etc.
provisions.summary: Lets the IA publish guidelines on its functions or on how the Ordinance operates. As with codes, a breach does not itself create liability, but a guideline is admissible and relevant provisions must be taken into account in court.
provisions.counselNote: Most of the IA's detailed expectations sit in guidelines such as GL23, GL24, GL25, GL29 and GL30. Each needs a current-version check before it is built into a product flow.

provisions.title: Inspection and investigation powers in relation to authorized institutions
provisions.summary: Limits an inspector's or investigator's power to require an authorized institution to disclose customer information. The power is available only to a specified authority, such as the Monetary Authority, or where the officer certifies that disclosure is necessary.
provisions.counselNote: A customer data request from the IA to the bank must pass these tests. Route any such request to legal and the data protection owner before responding.

provisions.title: Amount of levy
provisions.summary: Sets the levy payable on each premium payment on specified general and long term business. The levy is the premium multiplied by the rate for the policy year's period, subject to maxima per policy year. The Schedule sets the rate at 0.1% from 1 April 2021.
provisions.counselNote: Include the levy in pricing and in the customer's premium disclosure. Confirm with the insurer who collects and remits it.

provisions.instrument: Insurance Authority, Code of Conduct for Licensed Insurance Agents
provisions.title: Code of Conduct for Licensed Insurance Agents
provisions.summary: Issued by the IA under s.95 for licensed insurance agents. It sets practice standards for conduct toward clients, and a parallel code applies to licensed insurance brokers. Commentary reports that licensees had under three months to align systems after publication.
provisions.counselNote: Read the current agent code and its broker counterpart against the app's sales journey. Confirm the current edition before relying on any theme described here.

checklist: **Confirm the licence route:** Decide whether the bank holds a licence (as an agency or broker company) or acts through a licensed partner, and record the basis in a memo.
**Map the regulators:** List which matters go to the IA, which go to the HKMA under s.4G, and which go to others such as the SFC or PCPD.
**Build a rules register:** Track Cap. 41 provisions, s.94 rules, s.95 codes, s.133 guidelines and circulars, with dates and current status.
**Confirm the bank's register position:** Search the IA's registers by the bank's name and by its partner's name, rather than assuming a status.
**Check the levy in pricing:** Confirm the premium base and whether the levy applies to each product (Cap. 41J, ss.4-6).
**Set the correspondence protocol:** Route IA and HKMA notices to one named owner, with a log of each request and response.
**Diarise reform dates:** Track the RBC enhancements (proposed target 31 December 2026) and the Policyholders' Protection Scheme status.
**Agree the operating model with the insurer:** Settle early who holds the licence, owns the codes, sets the product and collects the levy.
itAngle: **Rules as data:** Codes and guidelines are published documents. Keep each version, its effective date and its source in a searchable repository, so the team can show which text applied on a given date.
**Licence records:** The IA register and the bank's own records of who sells what must match. Link agent identifiers to staff access rights in the app, and review the link when a licence changes.
**Levy computation:** The levy is a percentage of premium with a per-policy-year maximum, so the system must compute it per policy year and per premium payment (Cap. 41J, ss.4-6).
**Evidence of control:** Regulators will ask for system records. Plan to retrieve who saw which disclosure and when, quickly and in a form that holds up.
bankNotes: **No general bank exemption:** s.78 exempts authorized insurers only, and s.78(2) does not extend that to their agents. A bank carrying on regulated activities is caught by s.64G unless it holds a licence, acts through a licensed intermediary, or falls within an exception in s.64G(3) or s.123 (for example, clerical duties under s.123(2)). Confirm each exception before launch.

**HKMA by delegation:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over the bank's insurance intermediary business to the [[Monetary Authority]] (s.4G), and can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining an authorized institution (s.64ZZH(2); ss.82(4), 84(4)).

**Limits on customer data requests:** s.64ZZJ restricts what an IA inspector or investigator can demand from a bank about customers. The bank must not treat a bare IA request as a licence to hand over customer records.

**Winding-up protection:** s.76(1) stops the IA petitioning to wind up an intermediary that is an authorized institution. The bank's own insolvency is governed by the banking regime, which this stage does not cover.
pitfalls: **Assuming the HKMA alone regulates:** The IA still licenses, issues codes under s.95 and can discipline under s.81. Treating the HKMA as the only channel is a mistake.
**Treating codes as optional:** Under s.95(6), a breach can count against fitness and properness, even though it does not by itself create liability.
**Underestimating the offence:** Carrying on a regulated activity without the right licence exposes the individuals and the company to penalties under s.64G(4), including imprisonment on indictment.
**Treating 2019 as one date:** Codes and guidelines started on different dates, and many have been revised since. Check each commencement date and current version.

glossary.definition: The statutory body established under Part IA of Cap. 41 to regulate and supervise the insurance industry, including the licensing of intermediaries (s.4A).
An insurer authorized under Part II of Cap. 41 to carry on insurance business. The term is not the same as an authorized institution.

A person holding one of the five licences under Part X: a licensed insurance agency, a licensed individual insurance agent, a licensed technical representative (agent), a licensed insurance broker company or a licensed technical representative (broker).
Negotiating or arranging a contract of insurance, inviting or inducing a person to enter one or to make a material decision, or giving regulated advice (s.3A and Sch. 1A, Pt 1).
A bank or other institution authorized under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155). Cap. 41 takes this meaning from BO s.2(1).
The head of the HKMA, which supervises authorized institutions under the Banking Ordinance and, by delegation, their insurance intermediary business.
The test the IA applies when licensing or continuing to license a person, covering qualifications, competence, reputation, financial standing and disciplinary history (s.64ZZA).
Guidance published under s.95 on the practices and standards licensed intermediaries are expected to follow. It is not subsidiary legislation.
Rules, regulations or orders made under a power in an Ordinance, such as the levy order in Cap. 41J, which have legal force in their own right.

title: Insurance business, regulated activities & the perimeter
oneLiner: Only authorized insurers may write insurance, and any app feature that invites, arranges or advises on a policy needs a licence or a clear exception.
keyPoints: **Insurers:** Under s.6(1) of the Insurance Ordinance (Cap. 41), only an authorized insurer, Lloyd's or an approved association of underwriters may carry on insurance business in or from Hong Kong.
**Regulated activities:** Negotiating or arranging a contract, inviting or inducing a purchase, inviting or inducing a material decision, and giving regulated advice are restricted by s.64G.

**Who may act:** Licensed insurance agencies, licensed individual agents, licensed broker companies and their licensed technical representatives may carry on these acts within their licence and appointment.

**The insurer's side:** An authorized insurer must not contract through, or accept a referral from, an unlicensed person in Hong Kong (s.64N). A contract made in breach of s.64N(1) can be enforced or voided at the policy holder's option.
**Exceptions:** Section 123 covers certain professionals, advice through public media, claims handling and clerical work. Each is narrow, and none covers selling in an app.
**Counsel's role:** Test every app feature against Schedule 1A before design, not after launch, and record the answer.

conceptMap.caption: How an app feature is tested against the perimeter. Each step is a question counsel should answer in writing.

deepDive.heading: What counts as insurance business
deepDive.lede: The first question is whether the bank would be carrying on an insurance class at all.
points: **Restriction:** Under s.6(1), no person may carry on any class of insurance business in or from Hong Kong unless authorized under s.8 or 8A, or is Lloyd's or an approved association of underwriters.
**Classes:** Schedule 1 lists long-term classes A to I and general classes 1 to 17. Section 3(2) deems some contracts that are not insurance to be insurance for the Ordinance.

**Offence:** Contravening s.6(1) is an offence. On indictment the fine is $2,000,000 and, for an individual, two years' imprisonment, with a further $2,000 for each day the offence continues (s.6(3)).

**Contract consequence:** Under s.6A, a contract entered into by an insurer in breach of s.6(1) is, at the policy holder's option, enforceable against the insurer or void. Reinsurance is excluded (s.6A(3)).
**Counsel's view:** The bank does not need to underwrite to be caught. Any role that amounts to carrying on the insurer's business needs to be confirmed as outside s.6(1).
deepDive.takeaway: Insurance business is reserved to authorized insurers, so the bank's role must always be that of an intermediary.

deepDive.heading: Regulated activities: the core test
deepDive.lede: Section 64G restricts certain acts, so the restriction reaches intermediaries as well as insurers.
points: **Acts (Sch. 1A, Pt 1):** Negotiating or arranging a contract, inviting or inducing a person to enter a contract, inviting or inducing a material decision, and giving regulated advice.

**Material decisions (Sch. 1A, Pt 2):** Applying for, issuing, renewing, cancelling, terminating, surrendering, assigning, exercising rights under, changing terms of, or making or settling a claim under a contract.
**Restriction (s.64G(1)-(2)):** No person may carry on a regulated activity in the course of business or employment, or for reward. No person may hold out that it does.

**Penalty (s.64G(4)):** Without reasonable excuse, a breach is an offence. On indictment the fine is $1,000,000 and two years' imprisonment, plus $20,000 a day for a continuing offence. On summary conviction the fine is level 6 and six months, plus $2,000 a day.
**Permitted persons (s.64G(3)):** Licensed agencies, agents, technical representatives and broker companies may act within their licence and appointment, with the limits set out in each paragraph.
deepDive.takeaway: An app feature that invites a purchase is a regulated activity even if no licensed person is in the loop.

deepDive.heading: The insurer's side: no unlicensed selling or referrals
deepDive.lede: Section 64N places the same limits on the insurer, which gives the policy holder a remedy.
points: **Contracting (s.64N(1)):** An authorized insurer must not enter into a contract through another person in Hong Kong unless that person is a licensed agency or agent appointed by it, a licensed broker company, or does only clerical or administrative work.
**Referrals (s.64N(2)):** The same limits apply to an insurer accepting a referral of insurance business from a person in Hong Kong.

**Remedy (s.64N(3)-(4)):** Only for a contract entered into in breach of s.64N(1): at the policy holder's option it is enforceable against the insurer or void. A referral breach under s.64N(2) gives no enforce-or-void right, although the insurer still commits an offence (s.64N(5)).
**Offence (s.64N(5)):** An insurer in breach commits an offence. On indictment the fine is $1,000,000 and two years' imprisonment. On summary conviction the fine is level 6 and six months.

**Practical effect:** A referral model under which an unlicensed bank sends customers to an insurer, for a fee or otherwise, falls within s.64N(2). IA guidance on referral fees is reported to add further limits, which are not covered here.
deepDive.takeaway: A bank that is not licensed cannot be the channel through which an insurer receives business.

deepDive.heading: Exceptions and exemptions
deepDive.lede: The exceptions in s.123 are narrow, and each depends on the person and the activity.
points: **Clerical work (s.123(2)):** A person acting for an insurer or licensed intermediary may discharge clerical or administrative duties only.

**Advice to the public (s.123(1)(f)):** Regulated advice given through a generally available publication, broadcast or electronic communication is exempt. Inviting or arranging a purchase is not covered.

**Claims (s.123(1)(g)):** Loss assessors may advise for an authorized insurer, policy holder or claimant, and claim settlers may advise for an authorized insurer, in that business. Holding out is covered too.
**Professionals (s.123(1)(a)-(e)):** Counsel, solicitors, certified public accountants, trust companies and actuaries may give regulated advice wholly incidental to their practice.

**Insurers (s.78, s.123(4)):** An authorized insurer need not be a licensed intermediary to carry on regulated activities, but its agents are not covered by that exemption (s.78(2)). Employees may assess risks, set terms and process claims (s.123(4)).
**Authority exemptions (s.79):** The Authority may grant an exemption on application, with conditions and a validity period, and may revoke it.
deepDive.takeaway: Do not rely on an exception without confirming the person, the activity and any condition attached to it.

deepDive.heading: Reaching into Hong Kong and neighbouring regimes
deepDive.lede: Where the insurer sits, and what the product is called, do not take a feature outside the perimeter.
points: **In or from Hong Kong (s.6(1)):** The restriction applies to business carried on in or from Hong Kong, so the insurer's location and the customer's location both matter.
**Marketing from abroad (s.64H):** Actively marketing insurance services to the public from outside Hong Kong is treated as holding out for s.64G(2).

**Overseas insurers:** An insurer not authorized here cannot carry on business in or from Hong Kong (s.6(1)). A bank that offers its policies through the app also needs a permitted route under s.64G, and s.64N applies to the insurer.

**Investment-linked products (SFO s.103):** SFC guidance reports that intermediaries dealing solely in ILAS and other insurance products generally need no SFO licence. Other securities business can trigger a licence. Confirm the current Licensing Handbook position before relying on it.

**Other perimeters:** Deposits and structured deposits fall under banking rules. MPF products and premium financing need their own review, and the Money Lenders Ordinance (Cap. 163) needs checking against the current text.
deepDive.takeaway: Each neighbouring product needs its own perimeter check, because the labels do not carry over.

provisions.title: Restriction on carrying on of insurance business
provisions.summary: Bars anyone from carrying on any class of insurance business in or from Hong Kong unless authorized under s.8 or 8A, or is Lloyd's or an approved association of underwriters. Contravention is an offence with a fine of $2,000,000 and up to two years' imprisonment on indictment, plus a daily fine.
provisions.counselNote: The bank must never act as an unauthorized risk carrier. Confirm the insurer is authorized before any product screen is built.

provisions.title: Contracts of insurance entered into in contravention of section 6(1)
provisions.summary: A contract entered into by an insurer in breach of s.6(1) is, at the policy holder's option, either enforceable against the insurer or void. A policy holder who voids it before expiry can recover the consideration paid. Reinsurance contracts are not void for this reason alone.
provisions.counselNote: The policy holder, not the regulator, chooses the remedy. A partner's breach can therefore leave the bank with a claim it did not expect.

provisions.title: Classes of insurance business
provisions.summary: The classes relevant to the Ordinance are those in Schedule 1. Certain contracts that are not otherwise insurance, including some tontines and retirement-scheme contracts, are deemed to be contracts of insurance.
provisions.counselNote: Product labels do not decide the class. Map each product to its Schedule 1 class before deciding which perimeter rules apply.

provisions.title: Classes of Insurance Business
provisions.summary: Lists long-term classes A to I (life and annuity, linked long term, permanent health, tontines, capital redemption, and retirement schemes) and general classes 1 to 17 (from accident and sickness through legal expenses).
provisions.counselNote: **Class check:** Check each product's class against this list. Class C covers linked long-term business, which stage 8 treats in detail.

provisions.title: Regulated activity, material decision and regulated advice
provisions.summary: Defines the three concepts used throughout the regime by reference to Schedule 1A: an act in Part 1, a decision in Part 2, and an opinion in Part 3.
provisions.counselNote: Every app feature should be described in these three terms before it is assessed.

provisions.title: Regulated Activity, Material Decision and Regulated Advice
provisions.summary: Part 1 lists four acts: negotiating or arranging, inviting or inducing a contract, inviting or inducing a material decision, and giving regulated advice. Part 2 lists the material decisions, and Part 3 lists the matters on which advice is regulated.
provisions.counselNote: The list is wide. A comparison widget, a suggested product or a nudge towards a purchase can each be an act under Part 1. Test each against it.

provisions.title: Restrictions on carrying on regulated activities
provisions.summary: Prohibits carrying on a regulated activity in the course of business or employment, or for reward, and holding out as doing so. Section 64G(3) permits licensed agencies, agents, technical representatives and broker companies to act within their licence and appointment. Breach without reasonable excuse is an offence.
provisions.counselNote: This is the core licence requirement for the bank. The bank needs one of the permitted roles, and each individual acting for it needs the matching licence.

provisions.title: Application of section 64G in relation to marketing insurance services outside Hong Kong
provisions.summary: A person who actively markets insurance services to the public from outside Hong Kong is treated as holding out that it carries on a regulated activity, for s.64G(2). This applies whether the person markets directly or through someone acting for it.
provisions.counselNote: Geo-restrict insurance pages or offers if the bank's overseas operations or partners market to Hong Kong residents.

provisions.title: Contracts of insurance made through persons other than licensed insurance intermediaries, etc.
provisions.summary: An authorized insurer must not contract through, or accept a referral from, a person in Hong Kong unless that person is a licensed agency or agent appointed by the insurer, a licensed broker company, or does only clerical or administrative work. A contract made in breach of the contracting limit (s.64N(1)) is, at the policy holder's option, enforceable against the insurer or void; a referral breach (s.64N(2)) gives no such right. The insurer commits an offence either way.
provisions.counselNote: The bank's route must be licensed before any referral is accepted. Section 64N(2) does not refer to fees, but IA guidance on referral fees is separate and should be checked before any fee arrangement is agreed.

provisions.title: Exceptions to sections 64G and 120
provisions.summary: Exempts certain professionals for advice incidental to their practice, regulated advice given through public media or electronic communication to the public, loss assessment and claims settling, specified group companies, clerical or administrative work for an insurer or intermediary, and insurer employees doing risk, terms or claims work.
provisions.counselNote: The public-media exception covers advice, not inviting a purchase. The clerical exception is narrow. Record which exception, if any, is relied on for each feature.

provisions.title: Exemptions for authorized insurers, etc.
provisions.summary: An authorized insurer does not need to be a licensed intermediary to carry on regulated activities or hold out that it does. The exemption does not extend to the insurer's agents.
provisions.counselNote: The bank cannot borrow the insurer's exemption. Any bank staff selling a policy need their own route under s.64G.

provisions.title: Offence to issue advertisements, invitations or documents relating to investments in certain cases
provisions.summary: Makes it an offence to issue an advertisement or invitation to the public to acquire certain securities, structured products or collective investment scheme interests, unless the issue is authorized by the SFC under s.105(1). Several intermediary exemptions apply. Whether ILAS are caught, and on what conditions, is reported; check the current text.
provisions.counselNote: Pointer only. Before offering any investment-linked product, confirm with the SFC or the IA whether s.103 applies, and what materials must be authorized.

checklist: **Inventory features:** List every app feature that touches insurance, including comparison tools, prompts, chat replies and pre-filled forms.
**Sch. 1A test:** For each feature, record whether it negotiates, arranges, invites, induces, advises or affects a material decision.
**Exception check:** For any feature that passes the test, check ss.78 and 123 and record the exception relied on, with its conditions.
**Licence route:** Confirm which licence or appointment covers the bank before go-live, such as a licensed insurance agency or a licensed broker company.
**Individuals:** Confirm which staff need a licence or must be licensed technical representatives under s.64G(3)(c) or (e).
**Insurer confirmation:** Confirm each insurer is authorized under s.8 or 8A and that the bank's route satisfies s.64N before any referral is accepted.
**Overseas check:** For any group or overseas insurer, confirm Hong Kong authorization and whether s.64H applies to the marketing.
**Record and review:** Keep the assessments on file, and re-run them whenever a feature, partner, insurer or product changes.
itAngle: **Feature tagging:** Tag each screen, prompt and chatbot reply against Sch. 1A. Treat an automated recommendation as regulated advice until counsel confirms otherwise.
**Release control:** Use feature flags so that no product screen can go live before the licence, the insurer's confirmation and the sign-off are in place.
**Audit trail:** Log which feature was assessed against which provision, by whom, and when, so that the bank can show its reasoning to the IA.
**Geo-controls:** Restrict insurance pages to Hong Kong users where marketing from outside Hong Kong could be caught by s.64H.
bankNotes: **Licence first:** The bank needs its own route into the regime, such as a licensed insurance agency appointed by an insurer or a licensed broker company, before any app screen invites a purchase. See stages 3 and 6.
**Clerical exception is narrow:** Staff who only process forms or administer policies for an insurer may fall under s.123(2). Staff who explain, recommend or invite a purchase do not.
**Overseas group insurers:** A group insurer based abroad cannot be sold through the app unless it is authorized in Hong Kong (s.6(1)), and s.64H applies to any marketing from outside Hong Kong.

**Authorized institution status:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases), and the IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)). Stage 6 covers the bank's own licensing.
pitfalls: **Referral model:** Receiving a fee for sending customers to an insurer, without a licence, can breach s.64N for the insurer and s.64G for the bank.
**Assuming the bank's licence covers all staff:** Each person who negotiates or arranges a policy needs their own licence or must act under a permitted appointment (s.64G(3)).
**Treating advice as exempt:** Section 123(1)(f) exempts advice in public media. It does not cover inviting a purchase in the same article, banner or chat.
**Ignoring overseas products:** A product sold by a group insurer from abroad into Hong Kong stays in scope through s.6 and s.64H.

**Banking exemption misread:** Cap. 41 s.51(f) exempts a bank only as an insurer for specified classes and only for its banking business. It does not permit the bank to sell or refer insurance (see s.64G).

glossary.definition: An act listed in Part 1 of Schedule 1A: negotiating or arranging a contract, inviting or inducing a contract or material decision, or giving regulated advice (s.3A(a)).
A decision listed in Part 2 of Schedule 1A, such as applying for, renewing, cancelling, changing or claiming under a contract of insurance (s.3A(b)).
An opinion on a matter in Part 3 of Schedule 1A, which covers the same kinds of decision as material decisions (s.3A(c)).
Presenting oneself as carrying on a regulated activity. Caught by s.64G(2), and by s.64H for marketing from outside Hong Kong.
A business licensed under Cap. 41 to carry on regulated activities as agent of one or more authorized insurers that appointed it (s.64G(3)(a), s.64U(1), (5)(b)).
A company licensed under Cap. 41 that may act as agent of the policy holder for regulated activities (s.64G(3)(d)).
Work that only processes or administers for an insurer or intermediary. It is narrow and is not a route to selling (s.123(2)).
A company authorized under s.8 or 8A to carry on a class of insurance business in or from Hong Kong (s.6(1)(a)).
The person who holds a contract of insurance. Cap. 41 writes the term as two words, and the remedies in ss.6A and 64N belong to this person.

title: The digital bank's route into insurance
oneLiner: A digital bank can sell insurance in its app through a licensed agency or broker company, or by another route that counsel has confirmed the Ordinance allows.
keyPoints: **Licence first:** Under the [[Insurance Ordinance]] (Cap. 41), an app screen that invites or induces a purchase, or gives regulated advice, is a regulated activity. The bank must hold a licence or fit an exception (s.64G).

**Two licensed routes:** A licensed insurance agency acts for one or more insurers. A licensed insurance broker company acts for the customer. One entity cannot hold both licences (s.64U(5)(c), s.64ZA(4)(e)).
**Insurer gatekeeping:** An authorized insurer may not write business through, or accept a referral from, an unlicensed person, unless that person's role is clerical or administrative (s.64N(1)-(2)).

**Two regulators:** The [[Insurance Authority]] (IA) licenses and disciplines the bank and its people. The HKMA inspects and investigates the bank's insurance business under powers the IA delegated in 2019 (s.4G), and supervises the bank as a whole under the Banking Ordinance.
**People count:** Each individual who advises, arranges or induces a purchase needs a [[technical representative]] licence. The entity also needs an approved [[responsible officer]] (s.64Y, s.64ZE).
**Counsel's role:** Choose the model before the app journey is designed. The model fixes the licences, the insurer contracts and the conduct duties.

deepDive.heading: Why a licence is unavoidable
deepDive.lede: The app is the sales channel, so the Ordinance reaches it directly.
points: **Scope of s.64G:** A person must not carry on a regulated activity in the course of business or for reward. Regulated activities are negotiating or arranging a contract, inviting or inducing a person to enter a contract or make a material decision (such as a change, surrender or claim), and giving regulated advice (Sch. 1A, Pt 1, para 1).

**Penalty:** Without reasonable excuse, a breach is an offence. On indictment the fine is $1,000,000 and imprisonment is up to 2 years, with a further daily fine for a continuing offence (s.64G(4)(a)).

**No bank exemption found:** Cap. 41 has no general exemption for an authorized institution acting as an intermediary. Section 51(f) exempts an authorized institution only for specified classes of insurance business carried on solely for its banking business. It does not cover selling or referring insurance.

**Referrals:** Section 64N(2) bars an authorized insurer from accepting a referral from an unlicensed person. A bank that passes leads to an insurer is caught. Breach is an offence for the insurer (s.64N(5)). The policy holder's enforce-or-void option in s.64N(3) arises only where the contract itself is entered into in breach of s.64N(1).

**Clerical exception:** Section 123(2) protects a person acting on behalf of an insurer or licensed intermediary, where the work is only clerical or administrative. It does not cover inviting a purchase or giving advice, and it does not help a bank acting for itself.
deepDive.takeaway: Treat every app journey that invites, induces or advises as a regulated activity until counsel clears it.

deepDive.heading: The models compared
deepDive.lede: Five routes exist, and only the first two give the bank a licensed channel of its own.

items.label: (a) Licensed agency
items.note: Acts for insurers; up to 4 insurers, 2 long term

items.label: (b) Licensed broker company
items.note: Acts for the customer; capital and client money rules

items.label: (c) Partner or group insurer
items.note: Insurer authorized; sales still need a licensed channel

items.label: (d) Referral to a partner
items.note: Lawful only if clerical, or the bank is licensed

items.label: (e) Embedded or group cover
items.note: IA position unclear for a bank as policy holder

points: **(a) Agency:** An agency may act as agent of any authorized insurer (s.64U(1)). It must be appointed by at least one insurer (s.64U(5)(b)). Cap. 41K r.3 caps appointments at 4 insurers, no more than 2 for long term business. Rule 4 sets the counting; an insurer's long-term-only appointment counts as one long term insurer.

**(b) Broker:** A broker company may act as agent of the policy holder or potential policy holder (s.64ZA(1)(a)). It must meet capital, professional indemnity, separate client account and book-keeping rules made under s.129 (s.64ZA(4)(d)). The detailed Cap. 41L rules set the capital, indemnity and client money requirements. Read them before costing a broker route.

**(c) Partner insurer:** Authorization under s.8 requires fit and proper directors and controllers (s.8(2)). Appointing a controller needs IA approval (s.13A). An insurer's own staff are protected only for risk assessment, terms and claims (s.123(4)), so a sales role needs separate analysis.

**(d) Referral:** Section 64N(2) binds the insurer, not the bank. For the bank, a referral that invites or induces a purchase is a regulated activity unless its role is clerical or it is licensed (s.64G, s.123(2)). A bank that refers leads for a fee is not doing clerical work.

**(d) Guidance to read:** Read the IA's 2019 explanatory note for banks, prepared with the HKMA and the Hong Kong Association of Banks, before designing any referral journey. Its treatment of referrals is reported to make a bank's referral a regulated activity where the bank steers customers to one licensed intermediary's product or earns direct remuneration for it (reported; check the current text).
**(e) Embedded or group cover:** The IA's position is unclear. Whether a bank buying cover as policy holder falls outside s.64G needs checking. Ask the IA before relying on it.

deepDive.heading: Approvals and who gives them
deepDive.lede: The IA approves the entity and each person; the HKMA supervises the bank's business.

items.label: Entity licence
items.note: IA grants after a fit and proper test

items.label: Responsible officer
items.note: Must be a licensed TR, or applying for one

items.label: Technical representatives
items.note: Each individual who advises, arranges or induces

items.label: Insurer appointment
items.note: IA notified at least 14 days ahead

points: **Entity licence:** The IA may grant an agency licence only if the applicant is fit and proper, is appointed by an insurer, and files with it the technical representative and responsible officer applications that s.64U(3) requires, which must meet their own criteria (s.64U(5)(d)).

**Responsible officer:** An RO must be a licensed TR (agent), or applying for one, and fit and proper. The agency must give the RO authority and resources (s.91(1)(c)-(d)), which is also a condition of approval (s.64ZE(4)(c)).

**Technical representatives:** Only individuals can hold these licences (s.64Y(1)). A licensed TR (agent) may carry on regulated activities for the agency that appointed them, outside s.64G (s.64G(3)(c)). A broker TR has the parallel carve-out in s.64G(3)(e).
**Notices:** An insurer or agency must notify the IA at least 14 days before an appointment (s.64Q). Termination needs notice within 14 days (s.64R).

**HKMA:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases), and the IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)). The HKMA also supervises the bank as a whole under the Banking Ordinance, and its Supervisory Policy Manual module IB-1 sets its expectations for authorized institutions' insurance intermediary business (reported; check the current version). Check the current approval and its conditions before relying on the delegation for a new line.
deepDive.takeaway: The IA licenses the entity and each individual, and the HKMA supervises the bank's intermediary business.

deepDive.heading: What changes for a digital bank
deepDive.lede: With no branches, the app becomes the agency's sales channel, and its design carries legal weight.
points: **Software holds no licence:** A TR licence goes to an individual (s.64Y(1)). Any chat, video or human agent who advises, arranges or induces a purchase needs a TR licence, whatever the channel.

**Scripts and algorithms are conduct:** The agency must maintain controls to secure compliance with the s.90 conduct duties by itself and its TRs (s.91(1)). The IA's codes of conduct under s.95 add practice standards for agents and brokers that apply to app journeys (effective 23 September 2019; check the current text). The RO must use best endeavours to ensure those controls exist and are observed (s.91(2)).

**Best interests in the app:** Section 90(a) requires honest, fair action in the best interests of the policy holder or potential policy holder. A default product tile or a recommendation rule is tested against that duty.
**Remote sales:** Video and other non-face-to-face sales of long-term products are governed by IA and HKMA circulars. These are covered in the digital stage.
**Bank controls are not enough:** A bank's existing customer identity and AML controls do not discharge the agency's own conduct and record duties. Map both sets separately.
deepDive.takeaway: Map every app step to a regulated activity and to the person or controlled process that performs it, before design freeze.

deepDive.heading: Choosing and contracting with insurer partners
deepDive.lede: The agency agreement fixes liability, exclusivity and data use.
points: **Liability:** Where one insurer appoints an agent, that insurer is liable for the agent's acts in dealings with clients, whether or not within the agent's authority (s.68(2)). With several insurers, liability depends on the scope of authority (s.68(3)-(4B)).

**Disclosure carve-out:** An insurer is not liable for an act outside the agent's authority if the agent disclosed that limit to the client before the client relied on the act, with the clarity and prominence a client would reasonably need (s.68(4C)). The court may weigh other factors (s.68(4D)).
**Contract terms:** A term in an agency agreement that affects the intermediary's best-interests duty is void (s.68A). Drafting cannot move that duty.
**Appointment count:** Test each new insurer against the Cap. 41K r.3 cap of 4 insurers and 2 long term insurers, using the rule 4 counting.

**Commission and conflicts:** Section 90(f) requires the intermediary to use its best endeavours to avoid conflicts, and s.90(g) requires disclosure of any conflict that remains. Commission design for the app and staff needs that analysis.
**Data sharing:** Partner data flows and direct marketing consent sit under the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (Cap. 486). Mentioned only; see the digital stage.
deepDive.takeaway: Test every partner term against s.68 and s.68A before signing.

deepDive.heading: Timeline and the approval sequence
deepDive.lede: Licences, appointments and HKMA engagement can run in parallel, but the entity licence depends on its people.

points: **Sequence:** Decide the model, file TR and RO applications, apply for the entity licence, notify insurer appointments, engage the HKMA, then launch.

**Renewal:** An agency licence is valid for 3 years unless the IA sets another period (s.64V). A renewal application must be made no later than 45 days before expiry (s.64ZV(3)), so diary that date early.
**Broker add-ons:** A broker company must appoint an auditor within 1 month of its licence and file audited accounts within 6 months of year end (s.72(1), s.73(1)). Build both into the plan.

**HKMA consultation:** The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining an authorized institution or its agent (s.64ZZH(2), s.82(4), s.84(4)). Early HKMA dialogue on a new line is good practice. HKMA circulars on selling protection linked plans (8 July 2022 and 30 August 2023) are reported to expect a bank to discuss an ILAS launch with the HKMA beforehand (reported; check both circulars).
deepDive.takeaway: File the RO application with the entity application, plus a TR (agent) application unless the RO is already a licensed TR (s.64U(3)).

provisions.title: Restrictions on carrying on regulated activities
provisions.summary: Bars carrying on a regulated activity in the course of business or for reward, and holding out as doing so. Agencies, individual agents, broker companies and TRs are carved out for their own appointed roles. Breach is an offence.
provisions.counselNote: This is the entry point for any app journey. Agency and broker carve-outs apply only to licensed entities acting within their licences.

provisions.title: Contracts of insurance made through persons other than licensed insurance intermediaries, etc.
provisions.summary: An authorized insurer may not write contracts through, or accept referrals from, an unlicensed person in Hong Kong, unless that person's duties are only clerical or administrative. A contract made in breach is enforceable or void at the policy holder's option.
provisions.counselNote: A bank that refers app leads to an insurer must be licensed or clerical. Insurer contracts need an insurer-side check of the referral flow.

provisions.title: Exceptions to sections 64G and 120
provisions.summary: Excludes from s.64G a person acting for an authorized insurer or licensed intermediary where the regulated activity only involves clerical or administrative duties for it.
provisions.counselNote: The exception is narrow. Product explanations, prompts and recommendations are not clerical, so the exception should not carry an app's sales journey.

provisions.instrument: Insurance (Maximum Number of Authorized Insurers) Rules (Cap. 41K)
provisions.title: Maximum number of authorized insurers
provisions.summary: A person may be appointed for regulated activities by at most 4 authorized insurers, of which no more than 2 may be insurers authorized for long term business. Rule 4 explains how appointments are counted.
provisions.counselNote: This cap limits how many insurer partners an agency can carry. Check it before each new appointment. The text is dated 19 March 2020; check that it is current.

provisions.title: Grant of licence (insurance agency)
provisions.summary: Lets a sole proprietor, partnership or company apply for an agency licence to act as agent of any authorized insurer. The IA must be satisfied on fitness and propriety, insurer appointment, that the applicant does not hold a broker licence, and the accompanying TR or RO applications.
provisions.counselNote: The entity cannot be a licensed agency and a broker company at the same time. Appointment by an insurer is needed before the licence is granted, so partner timing matters.

provisions.title: Validity of insurance agency licence
provisions.summary: An agency licence runs for 3 years from grant, or another period the IA sets for a particular case.
provisions.counselNote: Diary renewal well ahead. The renewal process for entities still needs checking with the IA.

provisions.title: Grant of licence (insurance broker company)
provisions.summary: Lets a company apply for a broker licence to act as agent of a policy holder or potential policy holder, and to carry on invitation and advice activities. The IA must be satisfied on fitness and propriety and on the company's ability to meet rules made under s.129 on capital, professional indemnity, client accounts and books.
provisions.counselNote: The broker route makes the company the customer's agent (s.64ZA(1)(a)). The capital, indemnity and client money rules need a costed plan.

provisions.title: Approval of responsible officers of licensed insurance agencies
provisions.summary: A licensed agency, or an applicant for one, may apply for approval of an individual as responsible officer. The individual must be a licensed TR (agent), or applying for one, and must be fit and proper with sufficient authority and resources.
provisions.counselNote: The RO is the named accountable person for the agency's conduct controls. Pick the individual early, and check that the bank's governance supports the role.

provisions.title: Authorized insurer's relationship with its agent
provisions.summary: Makes an insurer liable for its agent's acts in dealings with clients, whether or not within authority. Liability is shared where the agent is appointed by several insurers. An insurer can escape liability for out-of-scope acts only if the agent clearly disclosed the limit before reliance.
provisions.counselNote: The partner insurer carries much of the front-end conduct risk, so the agreement and disclosure design shape who bears what.

provisions.title: Validity of agency agreements
provisions.summary: A provision in an agency agreement that affects an intermediary's duty under s.90(a) is void.
provisions.counselNote: Partner contracts cannot dilute the best-interests duty. Review every waiver or limitation clause against this section.

provisions.title: Delegation of certain powers of Authority to Monetary Authority
provisions.summary: The IA may delegate its s.64ZZF(6) and s.64ZZH(1) powers to the Monetary Authority for an authorized institution's regulated activity, subject to Chief Executive in Council approval and conditions.
provisions.counselNote: The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases), and the IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)). The HKMA also supervises the bank as a whole under the Banking Ordinance, and its Supervisory Policy Manual module IB-1 sets its expectations for authorized institutions' insurance intermediary business (reported; check the current version). Confirm the current approval and its conditions.

provisions.title: Conduct requirements for licensed insurance intermediaries
provisions.summary: A licensed intermediary must act honestly, fairly and in the best interests of the policy holder, with care and skill, advise only within competence, consider the customer's circumstances, make necessary disclosure, avoid conflicts or disclose them, and account promptly for client assets.
provisions.counselNote: These duties apply to the app, its scripts and its staff. They should shape product selection, default options and disclosure screens from the outset.

checklist: **Pick the model:** Record why agency, broker or partner insurer was chosen. Check the single-entity rule (s.64U(5)(c), s.64ZA(4)(e)) and the Cap. 41K count.
**Map app journeys:** List each screen that invites, induces or advises, and name the person or controlled process that performs it.
**Licence roles:** Confirm the RO and each TR candidate. File the RO application with the entity application, plus a TR application unless the RO is already a licensed TR (s.64U(3)).
**Insurer appointments:** Diary the 14-day prior notice for each appointment (s.64Q) and the 14-day notice on termination (s.64R).
**Agency terms:** Check each agency agreement against s.68 and s.68A, and the 4-insurer, 2-long-term cap.
**Conduct controls:** Build the s.90 duties and the s.91 control and best endeavours duties into product and journey design.
**HKMA engagement:** Brief the HKMA early on the model and the app journey, and record what it says.

**Renewal and records:** Calendar the 3-year validity (s.64V) and the renewal application 45 days before expiry (s.64ZV(3)). For a broker company, calendar the auditor appointment and audited accounts (s.72(1), s.73(1)).
itAngle: **Journey mapping:** Treat each app step as a regulated activity with a named owner, a record and a control. Logs of what the customer saw will matter in any complaint or inquiry.
**Software holds no licence:** Licences attach to entities and individuals. Record which licensed person or process was responsible for each recommendation.
**Partner data flows:** Insurer feeds, consent records and direct marketing need the PDPO analysis in the digital stage.
**Change control:** Scripts, rules and algorithms that affect best interests or needs analysis are conduct changes. Route them through compliance and the RO as good practice.
bankNotes: **No general bank exemption found:** The banking licence does not by itself authorize insurance intermediation. The bank needs its own IA licence or a clear s.123 route.

**Two supervisors:** The IA licenses the entity and its people. The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases), and the IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)). The HKMA also supervises the bank as a whole under the Banking Ordinance, and its Supervisory Policy Manual module IB-1 sets its expectations for authorized institutions' insurance intermediary business (reported; check the current version).
**Winding up:** The IA cannot petition to wind up a licensed intermediary that is an authorized institution (s.76(1)).

**Existing bank agencies:** Press reports describe some Hong Kong virtual banks holding IA agency licences and acting for named insurers, for example ZA Bank (reported around 2021) and PAObank (reported March 2025). The IA register should be searched by bank name before this is relied on.
pitfalls: **Unlicensed leads:** Passing app leads to an insurer for a fee, where the bank is unlicensed and its role is not clerical, puts the insurer in breach of s.64N(2). The bank's own conduct may be a regulated activity under s.64G. Referral to a licensed broker company is not caught by s.64N(2).
**Unlicensed staff:** Staff who explain products or recommend cover need TR licences. Relabelling a sales role as support does not remove that need.
**Stretching the clerical exception:** Section 123(2) covers administrative work only. Product explanations, sales prompts and recommendations fall outside it.

**Referral fees (reported; check):** IA guidance of 1 September 2025 reportedly tightens referral fees on participating policies. Reports say a benchmark applies and that arrangements with HKMA, SFC or MPF regulated entities are exempt. Check the circular for the benchmark and the exemption before relying on either.

glossary.definition: Cap. 41, the statute regulating insurers and intermediaries in Hong Kong. Its licensing and conduct rules apply to banks that distribute insurance.
The IA, the statutory regulator that licenses insurers and intermediaries under Cap. 41.
An entity licensed under s.64U to carry on regulated activities as agent of one or more authorized insurers.
An entity licensed under s.64ZA to carry on regulated activities for the customer, subject to capital, indemnity and client money rules.
An individual licensed under s.64Y (agent) or s.64ZC (broker) to carry on regulated activities for a licensed entity.
An individual approved under s.64ZE or s.64ZF to carry on accountability for an entity's conduct controls and compliance.
A bank or other institution authorized under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155), defined for Cap. 41 by s.2 by reference to that Ordinance.
