intro: This kit answers one question: can a digital bank offer or resell insurance in its app, and what must it obtain first? It covers the choice of distribution model, the licences and people, insurer partners, HKMA engagement, launch and duties after launch.

A digital bank is an authorized institution under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155). That status does not allow it to sell insurance. Cap. 41 has no general exemption for banks, so the bank needs its own licence (as an agency or a broker company) and its staff need technical representative licences, unless a specific exception applies.

Each activity card gives the route, the requirements, the gates Legal must clear and what to watch. Read the route line first, then the sources. Statute sections link to the official text, and every other source shows its legal force.
The kit does not cover product design, customer journeys in detail, or insurer-side rules. Those sit in the selling, digital and insurers stages.

triage.caption: The order a digital bank should work in, from the app audit to the first renewal.

items.label: Map each app feature against Sch. 1A
items.note: Sch. 1A, Pt 1 lists the regulated acts, including inviting or inducing a person to enter a contract of insurance. s.64G(1) bars carrying them on in the course of business or for reward, and s.64G(4) makes a breach without reasonable excuse an offence.

items.label: Confirm the clerical exception covers nothing sold
items.note: s.64N(1)(b) and s.123(2) exempt only purely clerical or administrative duties. Quotes, product choice and sales steps fall outside both exemptions.

items.label: Choose the distribution model
items.note: The options are an agency licence (s.64U), a broker company licence (s.64ZA) or a referral model. Cap. 41K r.3 limits a licensed person to appointments by up to 4 insurers, no more than 2 for long-term business (check the current text).

items.label: Apply for the licence with its people
items.note: An agency licence application must be accompanied either by a technical representative application and a responsible officer approval application, or by a responsible officer approval application for a licensed technical representative (s.64U(3)). A technical representative can be appointed by an applicant for the agency licence (s.64Y(3)(b)(ii)), so the individual and entity filings can be prepared together. Staff who sell or advise need their own licences (s.64Y).

items.label: Secure insurer appointments and notify the IA
items.note: Where one insurer appoints the agent, that insurer is liable for the agent's acts in its dealings, even outside its authority (s.68(2)). Where several insurers appoint the agent, s.68(3) to (4B) allocate liability, and s.68(4A) and (4B) make the appointing insurers jointly and severally liable in the cases they describe. Agreement terms that cut across the agent's s.90(a) duty are void (s.68A).

items.label: Engage the HKMA on supervision and governance
items.note: The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases). The IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)).

items.label: Build conduct controls and sales journeys
items.note: Codes of conduct issued under s.95 and IA guidelines such as GL30 on financial needs analysis set the standard. These are statutory guidelines, so confirm their current texts before design sign-off.

items.label: Set data, AML and record-keeping controls
items.note: Customer data and direct marketing fall under the PDPO (Cap. 486). AML/CFT duties sit under AMLO (Cap. 615). Inspectors can require records to test compliance (s.64ZZF), and s.64ZT can require records to go to clients after a licence is revoked or suspended.

items.label: Launch under HKMA and IA oversight
items.note: Legal signs off the licence, the appointments, the HKMA position and the conduct controls in writing before go-live. The board's approval of the business line should be recorded on the same file.

items.label: After launch: renewals, notices and inspections
items.note: An agency licence is valid for 3 years unless the IA sets another period (s.64V), and a renewal application must be made no later than 45 days before expiry (s.64ZV(3)). Insurers must notify the IA at least 14 days before appointing an agency (s.64Q(1)) and within 14 days after terminating one (s.64R(1)).

workplan.heading: Perimeter and model
workplan.lede: Settle what the app does, then choose the legal route that fits it.
points: **Feature mapping:** Test each feature, including banners, product pages, comparison tools, chat, quotes and renewal prompts, against Sch. 1A, Pt 1. Arranging a contract is also caught, and the IA explanatory note reads it widely (reported; check). Inviting or inducing a purchase is caught even if no sale completes.
**Clerical limit:** s.64N(1)(b) and s.123(2) cover only clerical or administrative work for an insurer or intermediary. Product advice and quote generation do not fit inside them.

**Bank exemption:** Section 51(f) exempts an authorized institution only for classes G or H, classes 16 and 17, or groups 1, 7 and 11 of Schedule 1, and only where it carries on that business solely for its banking business. This concerns the bank's own insurance business, not selling or referring a third party's cover, so record Legal's reading before relying on it.
**Model choice:** Compare the agency, the broker company, a partner-led referral model and the bank as policy holder. Each carries different licences, liability and conduct duties.
**Agency limits:** Cap. 41K r.3 allows up to 4 appointing insurers, with no more than 2 for long-term business. Count the group rules before choosing partners.

**Referral risk:** s.64N(2) stops an insurer accepting a referral from an unlicensed person in Hong Kong. A referral-only design therefore fails unless the bank holds a licence or the role is clerical. Reported bank guidance (IA, HKMA and HKAB, 2019) also treats a bank's referral as regulated activity where it steers customers to one intermediary's product or earns a payment for the referral (reported; check).

workplan.heading: Licences and people
workplan.lede: The licence is granted to the entity, but the people who sell and approve must be licensed or approved too.
points: **Entity licence:** An agency application under s.64U must be accompanied either by a technical representative application and a responsible officer application, or by a responsible officer application for a licensed technical representative (s.64U(3)). A licence is valid for 3 years unless the IA sets another period (s.64V).

**Responsible officers:** A responsible officer must be a licensed or applying technical representative, fit and proper, and given enough authority and resources (s.64ZE(4) for agencies, s.64ZF for broker companies).

**Technical representatives:** Staff who carry on regulated activities for the agency need technical representative licences (s.64Y). Automated journeys still belong to the agency, so the people who design, approve and supervise them must be checked.
**Fit and proper:** The IA assesses qualifications, experience and conduct when it decides fitness and propriety (s.64ZZA). Run the same checks on bank staff and directors before filing.
**Examination route:** Individual candidates usually sit the IIQE. The 70% pass mark and the two-year rule are reported from IA application notes; check them before planning training.

workplan.heading: Insurer partners and contracts
workplan.lede: The insurer carries much of the legal risk, so the agency agreement and the appointment process must be right from the start.
points: **Appointment notice:** The insurer must notify the IA in writing at least 14 days before appointing a licensed agency (s.64Q(1)). Build this into the partner timetable.
**Insurer liability:** Where one insurer appoints the agent, that insurer is liable for the agent's acts in the dealings, even outside the scope of authority (s.68(2)).
**Agreement terms:** A term that affects the agent's s.90(a) duty is void (s.68A). Review each partner agreement for clauses that limit the bank's duties to customers.
**Exclusivity and capacity:** Plan product lines against the 4-insurer and 2-long-term limits in Cap. 41K r.3, so that one partner does not block another.

**Commission and incentives:** Gifts, rebates and referral fees are limited by IA guidelines and circulars. The rebate rules and the 2025 referral-fee circular are reported, so check the originals before agreeing terms.

workplan.heading: HKMA, governance and the board
workplan.lede: The HKMA supervises the bank's insurance business under a delegation, so early engagement and clear governance matter.
points: **Delegated supervision:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases), and the IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining the bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)). Confirm the delegation's current terms with the HKMA.
**IA and HKMA consultation:** The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating a bank's insurance business (s.64ZZH(2)) or taking disciplinary action (ss.82(4), 84(4)).
**Customer records:** An inspector or investigator may require customer information only in the limited cases in s.64ZZJ. Set a protocol for how the bank responds to such requests.

**Pre-launch engagement:** Hold an HKMA discussion on model, target segment and channel before launch. HKMA circulars on selling protection linked plans (8 July 2022 and 30 August 2023) are reported to expect a bank to discuss an ILAS launch with the HKMA beforehand (reported; check both circulars).
**Board oversight:** Record the board's approval of the model, the partner contracts and the conduct policy. This is good practice, not a statutory test, but it evidences oversight.

workplan.heading: Customer journey and conduct controls
workplan.lede: The conduct duties are set by codes and guidelines, so the journeys must be tested against them, not against the marketing brief alone.
points: **Codes of conduct:** Codes for licensed agents and brokers are issued under s.95, and a breach can be weighed in a fit and proper assessment. Their effective date is reported as 23 September 2019; check it.
**Needs analysis:** IA guideline GL30 requires a financial needs analysis before a policy is recommended. Confirm the current text before designing the questions.

**Cooling-off:** IA guideline GL29 gives a cooling-off period of 21 calendar days for certain types of life insurance policies (its para 4.2 lists them; check the current text). It is a guideline under s.133, not law in itself. For other cover, check each policy's own cancellation terms.

**Remote sales:** HKMA circulars set risk-based alternatives to audio recording for video-conference sales (reported, December 2024). Confirm the current IA position on video sales of long-term products.

**Investment-linked products:** ILAS offers need SFC authorization under SFO s.104 and must meet the SFC Code on ILAS (reported; check the current Code). PLP sales follow HKMA circulars of 8 July 2022 and 30 August 2023, which are reported to expect a bank to discuss an ILAS launch with the HKMA beforehand (reported; check both circulars). Map each product to its regime before launch.

workplan.heading: Data, AML and records
workplan.lede: Customer data, consent and money-laundering controls run alongside the licence and must be designed in from the start.
points: **Data use and consent:** The PDPO (Cap. 486) governs sharing customer data with insurers and using it for direct marketing. Obtain consent for each purpose and keep the record.
**AML/CFT:** AMLO (Cap. 615) sets customer due diligence and reporting duties. Check the current IA AML/CFT guideline before relying on its detail.
**Records access:** Inspectors may require records under s.64ZZF. Keep sales, suitability and complaint records in a form that can be produced quickly.
**Record transfer:** If a licence is revoked or suspended, the IA may require copies of client records to be transferred to clients (s.64ZT). Plan the data export before it is needed.
**Cyber controls:** The IA cyber guideline GL20 applies to insurers, with a reported 72-hour notice duty. Check whether it reaches intermediaries, and the bank's own cyber obligations too.

workplan.heading: Launch and after launch
workplan.lede: Launch is a legal event as well as a product event, and the licence needs maintaining after it.
points: **Sign-off:** Legal confirms the licence, the approvals, the appointments, the HKMA position and the conduct controls in writing before go-live.
**Journey testing:** Test each live journey against Sch. 1A and the conduct controls. Keep the test evidence on the launch file.
**Renewals:** Agency licences run for 3 years unless the IA sets another period (s.64V). Renewal applications must be made no later than 45 days before expiry (s.64ZV(3)), so diarise that deadline.

**Notices:** Notify the IA of changes to particulars (s.64P), appointments (s.64Q) and terminations (s.64R). Appointment notices must be given at least 14 days before the appointment. Change and termination notices are due within 14 days after the event.
**Inspections and changes:** Expect HKMA or IA inspection under the delegated powers (s.4G, s.64ZZF). Review the controls after each product change and each change to the partner terms.

activities.title: Become a licensed insurance agency
activities.summary: An insurance agency acts for the authorized insurers that appoint it and sells their products to customers. It is the main licensed route for a bank that wants to sell insurance under its own name in the app.
activities.route: Yes. The bank applies to the IA for an insurance agency licence, which needs at least one authorized insurer to appoint it and a responsible officer who holds a technical representative (agent) licence. The licence is normally valid for three years, or another period the IA sets (s.64V), and covers only the lines of business it names.
require: **Licence application:** The bank applies under s.64U(1) for an agency licence covering long term business, general business or both. The IA may grant it only if the bank, its directors and any controller are fit and proper (s.64U(5)).

**Insurer appointment:** At least one authorized insurer must appoint the bank as its agent before the licence is granted (s.64U(5)(b)). The agency may carry on regulated activities only as agent of an insurer that has appointed it (s.64G(3)(a)).

**Responsible officer:** The agency needs an individual approved under s.64ZE. That person must be a licensed technical representative (agent), or be applying for one, and must have sufficient authority and resources within the agency (s.64ZE(4)).

**Staff licences:** Staff who carry on regulated activities for the agency must hold technical representative (agent) licences, which they obtain under s.64Y (s.64G(1)). Unlicensed staff must not carry on those activities in the course of their employment (s.64G(1)).

**Conduct controls:** The agency must maintain controls and procedures that secure compliance with the conduct duties in s.90, by itself and by its technical representatives, and must use best endeavours to make them observed (s.91(1)). The responsible officer has the matching duty (s.91(2)).

**Insurer liability:** The appointing insurer is generally liable for the agency's acts in dealings with clients, even outside the agency's authority (s.68), subject to the limited exceptions in s.68(4C).

**HKMA oversight:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases), and the IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)). The IA still licenses and disciplines the agency.
gates: **Confirm the lines of business:** Choose the long term and general lines the bank needs, because the licence covers only the lines it names (s.64U(1)). Later changes need approval under s.64S.
**Secure an appointment:** Get a signed agency appointment from at least one authorized insurer before filing, because the IA must be satisfied that it exists (s.64U(5)(b)).
**Name a responsible officer:** Choose a technical representative (agent) with real authority and resources, and file the approval application with the licence application (s.64U(3)).

**Count the insurer appointments:** Before adding any insurer, check the cap of 4 authorized insurers, of which no more than 2 may be long term (s.64I(1); Cap. 41K r.3). Insurers in the same group are counted under Cap. 41K r.5.
**Write the controls:** Document the controls and procedures required by s.91(1), covering app journeys, staff training, complaints and monitoring, and have the responsible officer sign them off.
**Diarise the licence term:** Note that the licence is normally valid for three years (s.64V). Calendar the renewal application, which must be made no later than 45 days before expiry (s.64ZV(3)).
watchFor: **Unlicensed selling in the app:** Staff or app features that recommend a policy without the right licence breach s.64G(1). The breach carries a fine and imprisonment (s.64G(4)).

**Products outside the appointment:** The agency may sell only the products of insurers that have appointed it (s.64G(3)(a)). Adding a new insurer's product without a new appointment falls outside the licence.
**Agency terms that cut across s.68:** Any term in an agency agreement that is inconsistent with s.68 is void (s.68(4E)), so insurer standard terms need checking.

activities.title: Become a licensed insurance broker company
activities.summary: A licensed insurance broker company acts as agent of the policy holder, so it can advise on and place cover with several insurers. The licence is heavier than an agency licence, with capital, client money, professional indemnity and audit duties.
activities.route: Yes. The bank would apply for a broker company licence under s.64ZA, which lets it act for policy holders and also invite, induce and advise. It needs an approved responsible officer, capital and net assets of at least HK$500,000 each, professional indemnity cover, a client account and an annual audit.
require: **Licence scope:** The company applies under s.64ZA(1) for a broker licence. It covers negotiating or arranging as agent of the policy holder (Sch. 1A Pt 1 item 1(a)), and inviting or inducing and giving regulated advice (items 1(b) to (d)), in the lines of business the licence names (s.64ZA(3)).

**Fitness and financial capacity:** The IA must be satisfied that the company, its directors and any controller are fit and proper, and that the company can comply with the capital, professional indemnity, client account and books rules (s.64ZA(4)(a) to (d)).

**Capital and insurance:** Paid-up share capital and net assets must each be at least HK$500,000 at all times (Cap. 41L rr.3 and 4). Professional indemnity cover must have a limit of at least the greater of twice brokerage income (capped at HK$75 million) and HK$3 million, with an automatic reinstatement (Cap. 41L r.5).
**Responsible officer:** The company needs an individual approved under s.64ZF. That person must be a licensed technical representative (broker), or be applying for one (s.64ZF(4)).

**Client money:** Client monies must be held apart from the company's own money, in a client account with an authorized institution, and reconciled at least monthly (s.71(1); Cap. 41L r.6). Client monies may be used only for the client they belong to (s.71(4)).

**Audit and records:** An auditor must be appointed within one month of the licence (s.72(1)). Audited accounts and an auditor's opinion on compliance with the capital, insurance, client account and books rules go to the IA within six months of each year end (s.73(1)). Records are kept for at least seven years (Cap. 41L r.7(3)).
gates: **Test the business case:** Confirm the bank needs a wider shelf, or a model without the four-insurer cap, before taking on the heavier licence. Compare the capital, insurance and audit cost with the agency route.
**Fund capital and net assets:** Confirm the company will keep at least HK$500,000 of paid-up share capital and net assets at all times, applying the intangible-asset exclusions in Cap. 41L r.4(2).

**Bind professional indemnity cover:** Obtain cover with the required limit and automatic reinstatement before the licence date, and check that the deductible is no more than 50% of net assets (Cap. 41L r.5(5)).

**Set up the client account:** Open an account at an authorized institution with the word client in its title, give the written notice required by Cap. 41L r.6(3), and set a monthly reconciliation (r.6(11)).
**Appoint the auditor and responsible officer:** Appoint the auditor within one month of the licence (s.72(1)), and file the responsible officer application under s.64ZF with the licence application.
**Plan the statutory calendar:** Diarise the six-month audit filing (s.73(1)) and the seven-year record retention period (Cap. 41L r.7(3)).
watchFor: **Staff overlap:** Under s.64K, a broker employee who manages regulated activities may not also be a licensed individual agent, a licensed technical representative (agent), or a proprietor or partner of an agency. A bank that runs both an agency and a broker company needs separate teams.

**Conflicts when the bank is the product seller:** A broker must use best endeavours to avoid conflicts with the policy holder and must disclose any it cannot avoid (s.90(f) and (g)). Presenting the bank's own tie-ups as neutral broker advice creates conflict risk.

**Client money misuse:** A lien or claim over client monies is void unless it covers fees then due to the company (s.71(6)). Any charge or mortgage over client monies is prohibited and void (s.71(7) and (8)). Breach of the client money rules is an offence (s.71(9)).

activities.title: Refer customers to an insurer or broker
activities.summary: Referring a customer to an insurer or broker becomes a regulated activity once the bank invites or induces the customer to buy, or negotiates or arranges the cover (Sch. 1A Pt 1 item 1). s.64G(1) then prohibits it in the course of business or for reward unless the bank is licensed. Insurers are also barred from taking referrals from unlicensed persons in Hong Kong, so the referral model affects the insurer as well as the bank.
activities.route: Only in a narrow form. A plain signpost that does not invite or induce, or give regulated advice, may fall outside Sch. 1A. A fee linked to sales is a risk factor that needs Legal's review, not a statutory test. A stronger referral needs the bank to hold an agency or broker licence, and an insurer may not accept a referral from an unlicensed person except for clerical or administrative work (s.64N(2)).
require: **Inviting or inducing:** Sch. 1A Pt 1 items 1(b) and (c) make inviting or inducing a person to enter a contract, or to make a material decision, a regulated activity. A referral that steers a customer toward a purchase can fall within s.64G(1).

**Insurer side:** An authorized insurer must not accept a referral of insurance business from a person in Hong Kong unless that person is a licensed agency, a licensed individual agent appointed by the insurer, a licensed broker company, or has only clerical or administrative duties (s.64N(2)).

**Offence and contract risk:** An insurer that accepts an unlawful referral commits an offence (s.64N(5)). A contract made through an unlicensed person under s.64N(1) is enforceable by the policy holder, or void at the policy holder's option (s.64N(3)).

**Clerical exception:** The exception covers clerical or administrative duties only (s.64N(2)(b); s.123(2)). Legal must judge whether the bank's role is only clerical. Leads passed on for sale are unlikely to qualify.

**Remuneration test:** Trade commentary on the IA's 2021 Explanatory Note on Regulated Activities says remuneration tied to sales, premiums or product numbers points towards regulated activity, while a flat fee points less that way (reported; check the note).

**Bank-specific steer:** The IA's 2019 explanatory note for banks, prepared with the HKMA and the Hong Kong Association of Banks, reportedly treats a referral as regulated activity where the bank encourages a customer toward one licensed intermediary's product, for example with preferential rates, or earns direct remuneration for the referral.
gates: **Choose the referral model:** Decide between a plain signpost, with no steer toward a product and no sales-linked fee, and a licensed route through an agency or broker licence. Record the decision and the reason.

**Check the receiving intermediary:** Before any referral, confirm the receiving party is a licensed agency, a licensed individual agent appointed by the insurer, or a licensed broker company (s.64N(2)).
**Remove sales-linked fees:** Confirm that no fee, commission or bonus moves with sales. If one does, treat the arrangement as likely regulated activity until Legal decides otherwise.
**Keep the steer neutral:** Check that app screens, offers and preferential rates do not favour one insurer or broker over others, in line with the IA's bank note (reported).

**Check the referral fee circulars:** Review any referral fee against the IA circulars of 2024 and 1 September 2025, which reportedly flag high fees (reported). Check the benchmark figure in the 2025 circular.
**Log every referral:** Record each referral, its trigger and any fee paid, and sample the records for steering or inducement.
watchFor: **Signpost turning into a pitch:** Pre-filled quotes, comparisons that narrow to one product, or staff scripts can turn a referral into inviting or inducing (Sch. 1A Pt 1 item 1(b)).
**Fee creep:** A flat fee that rises with volume or conversions moves towards sales-linked remuneration (reported).
**Insurer exposure:** The offence and the contract risk under s.64N fall on the insurer, so partner insurers will ask for assurance and may refuse referrals that are not clearly clerical.

activities.title: Sell a group or partner insurer's products, or own an insurer
activities.summary: A bank can sell a group or partner insurer's products only under its own licence, or it can own or form an insurer, which requires IA authorization and approval of controllers. Either route brings the agency rules, the cap on insurer appointments and the conflict rules into play.
activities.route: Yes, in two ways. To distribute a partner's products, the bank needs its own agency licence and an appointment (see the agency card). To own an insurer, the company needs IA authorization under s.8 and controller approvals under ss.13A and 13B, and the IA's Fast Track queue has been used by digital-only insurers, though its current scope needs checking with the IA (reported).
require: **Partner distribution:** The partner insurer appoints the bank as its agent (s.64U(5)(b)). The bank is a separate person from the insurer, so it still needs its own agency licence to sell the products (s.64G(1)).

**Authorization of an own insurer:** The company applies under s.7 for authorization to carry on long term or general business, and the IA may authorize it under s.8. The IA must refuse if a director or controller is not fit and proper (s.8(2)).

**Controllers:** The IA must approve an individual appointed as a controller, such as a managing director or chief executive (s.13A). A person who becomes a minority or majority shareholder controller needs prior IA approval (s.13B(2) and (2A)). A controller includes a managing director or chief executive, or a person whom the directors are accustomed to act on, or who holds 15% or more of the voting power (s.9(1)(a)).

**Fast Track for digital insurers:** The IA launched Fast Track in September 2017 as a queue for applicants that would sell only through digital channels. A December 2025 speech by the Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury reports four digital insurers authorized under it. The scope limits are reported and need checking.

**Group counting:** Under Cap. 41K r.5, appointments by insurers in the same group are counted as one or two insurers for the cap in s.64I and Cap. 41K r.3. This matters for an agency appointed by several group insurers.

**Conflicts of interest:** An intermediary must use best endeavours to avoid conflicts with the customer and must disclose any conflict it cannot avoid (s.90(f) and (g)). A bank that sells its own group insurer's cover must disclose that tie.
gates: **Pick the model:** Choose between partner distribution, which needs an agency licence and an appointment, and an owned insurer, which needs authorization. An owned insurer is a far larger project, so decide it at board level.

**Map the group appointments:** Confirm how each group insurer's appointment is counted under Cap. 41K r.5, and whether the bank stays within the cap of 4 authorized insurers, no more than 2 long term (s.64I(1); Cap. 41K r.3).

**Identify controllers early:** List every proposed managing director, chief executive, director and shareholder controller, and start their approvals under ss.13A and 13B early. Check the lead times with the IA.
**Confirm Fast Track eligibility:** Ask the IA whether a digital-only insurer fits Fast Track, and get the scope and conditions in writing, because the scope limits have only been reported so far.
**Disclose the group tie:** Set out the bank's interest in the insurer in product and app disclosures and in the conflicts policy (s.90(g)).
**Agree the partner terms:** Agree appointment terms, commission and insurer liability with the partner. A term inconsistent with s.68 is void (s.68(4E)), so check the wording.
watchFor: **Owning is not selling:** An owned insurer still cannot sell through the bank unless the bank holds its own agency licence (s.64G(1)).

**Unapproved share acquisition:** Acquiring minority or majority control without prior approval breaches s.13B(2) or (2A). A person who did not know of the breach must, within 14 days of becoming aware, notify the IA, apply for approval and pay the fee (s.13B(3) and (4)).

**Later group rules:** The Insurance (Amendment) Ordinance 2023 (enacted 6 July 2023) adds group-level approval points, including for a designated holding company. It commences by notice, so confirm which parts are in force before relying on this point (reported).

activities.title: Embedded cover and group policies the bank holds
activities.summary: A bank may bundle insurance with its own products, such as cover for card purchases, or hold a group policy in which the bank is the policy holder and its customers are the insured persons. Whether the bank carries on a regulated activity depends on what it does for those customers, not only on who holds the policy.
activities.route: It can be done, but only with the right licence or a design that keeps the bank's customer-facing steps outside regulated activity. The bank must decide whether it arranges, or invites or induces customers into cover. No IA guidance specific to this model has been identified, so Legal must make and document that judgement for each product.
require: **Regulated activity test:** Sch. 1A Pt 1 covers negotiating or arranging a contract (item 1(a)), and inviting or inducing a person to enter a contract or make a material decision (items 1(b) and (c)). Enrolling a customer, issuing a certificate or prompting an opt-in in the app can fall within these items.

**Policy holder and insured:** The bank is the policy holder under a group policy, and customers are the insured persons. Whether the bank carries on a regulated activity turns on its conduct toward those customers, not only on who holds the policy (s.64G(1)).

**Paid and free cover:** Where the bank earns commission, a margin or a fee from the cover, the for-reward test applies (s.64G(1)(b)). Free cover is not automatically outside the rules, because the bank may still act in the course of its business (s.64G(1)(a)).

**Insurer-side rule:** An authorized insurer must not enter a contract through a person in Hong Kong unless that person is licensed or its duties are only clerical or administrative (s.64N(1)). This matters where the bank handles enrolment for the insurer.

**Exceptions:** The clerical or administrative exception (s.123(2)) and the insurer-employee exception (s.123(4)) do not obviously cover bank staff who deal with customers on cover. Section 123(4) covers risk, terms and claims work only.
**Tied selling:** Whether a customer may be required to take cover with a loan or card, and what the Code of Banking Practice says on tied selling, need checking before launch.
gates: **Map each design:** For each product, record the policy holder, the insured persons, who enrols the customer, who pays the premium and who earns from it.
**Decide arranging:** Legal records its view on whether the bank arranges, or invites or induces, with reasons for each product.
**Licence or redesign:** If the bank performs those steps, obtain an agency or broker licence first, or redesign so the insurer or a licensed intermediary enrols the customer.
**Agree the insurer's position:** Get the insurer's written position on s.64N(1) and (2) before launch, because the insurer carries the offence risk.
**Confirm tied selling:** Check the Code of Banking Practice and any HKMA expectations on tied selling and bundling. Check these points before launch.
**Disclose the terms:** Show customers the cover, whether it is free or paid, and the bank's interest in it. Section 90(e) and (g) apply if the bank is a licensed intermediary.

**Check cooling-off rights:** IA guideline GL29 gives a cooling-off period of 21 calendar days for certain life policies (its para 4.2 lists them; check the current text). General cover follows each policy's own cancellation terms. Build cancellation and refund flows for any group certificate that falls within it.
watchFor: **Default enrolment:** Pre-ticked or default opt-in journeys in the app can amount to arranging, or inviting or inducing (Sch. 1A Pt 1 item 1(b)).
**Reward creep:** Any commission, margin or fee linked to the cover brings the bank within the for-reward test (s.64G(1)(b)).
**Analogy risk:** HKMA investor-protection circulars cover insurance and ILAS sales, but they do not settle the position for group embedded cover. Do not rely on analogy alone.

activities.title: Overseas insurers, non-residents and the Greater Bay Area
activities.summary: Only IA-authorized insurers, Lloyd's, or IA-approved associations of underwriters may carry on insurance business in or from Hong Kong. Active marketing of insurance to the Hong Kong public from outside Hong Kong is treated as holding out a regulated activity under s.64G(2) (s.64H). A bank must avoid that unless the activity is licensed. Mainland customers and Greater Bay Area service raise further questions that need local advice.
activities.route: Only with authorized insurers, and only from Hong Kong. The bank may not sell the products of an insurer the IA has not authorized, and active marketing to the Hong Kong public from outside Hong Kong counts as holding out (s.64H). Mainland rules are outside this kit; take mainland advice first.
require: **Authorized insurers only:** No person may carry on insurance business in or from Hong Kong unless it is authorized under s.8 or 8A, or is Lloyd's or an IA-approved association of underwriters (s.6(1)). A bank that sells an unauthorized insurer's cover also risks breaching s.64G(1).

**Contract status:** A contract entered into in breach of s.6(1) is, at the policy holder's option, either enforceable against the insurer or void (s.6A(1)). A policy holder who voids it may recover the consideration paid (s.6A(2)).

**Marketing from outside Hong Kong:** Actively marketing insurance services to the Hong Kong public from outside Hong Kong counts as holding out under s.64H(1). This applies whether the person markets or someone markets on its behalf (s.64H(2)).

**Group affiliates and agents:** Under s.64H(2), marketing done by someone on an offshore provider's behalf is treated as the provider's marketing, even if the bank did not do it. An overseas group company or agency that holds out in its own right also needs assessing under s.64G(2).

**Mainland visitors:** A 2016 IA circular requires an Important Facts Statement for new individual long-term applications from mainland visitors, from 1 September 2016 (reported; check the circular text).
**Greater Bay Area centres:** Insurers' after-sales centres in Nansha and Qianhai are reported to be for servicing policies only in the first phase, not for new sales (reported).
gates: **Check each insurer:** Check each partner insurer, including any non-Hong Kong insurer, against the IA register before its products appear in the app.
**Keep the sales route in Hong Kong:** Sales and advice should come from Hong Kong, under the bank's own licence, not from an offshore group entity.
**Review marketing:** Check every advert, social post and app banner aimed at Hong Kong customers for offshore origin, and check s.64H before any campaign runs from outside Hong Kong.
**Design the mainland visitor journey:** If the app serves mainland visitors, confirm the Important Facts Statement and the sign-off mechanism. Check the current requirements.
**Get mainland advice:** Obtain mainland legal advice before offering any product to mainland residents. Mainland rules are outside this kit.
**Confirm service scope:** Confirm in writing with each insurer what any Greater Bay Area service centre can do, and that it cannot sell new policies.
**Set location controls:** Decide how the app confirms that a customer applying for cover is in Hong Kong, and what happens if it cannot.
watchFor: **Unauthorized partner:** A product from an insurer the IA has not authorized may be void or enforceable at the customer's option (s.6A), and the bank's sales of it would be unlicensed.
**Customers who apply while abroad:** Legal should confirm how the rules apply to a Hong Kong customer who applies while travelling, because s.64H turns on active marketing from outside Hong Kong.
**Stale plans:** The Greater Bay Area centre plans date from 2019 and their current status needs checking. Do not treat them as in force.

activities.title: Responsible officer and licensed staff in a digital bank
activities.summary: A digital bank that sells insurance needs an insurance agency licence or a broker company licence, and its staff need the matching licences. The people who run the agency and deal with customers must hold the right licences, and the responsible officer must be approved by the IA. A digital journey with no human adviser does not remove these duties.
activities.route: Yes, through an insurance agency licence (applied for under s.64U) with an IA-approved responsible officer. Each technical representative (agent) needs a licence under s.64Y and an appointment by that agency. Appointments and exits must be notified to the IA within the time limits in ss.64Q and 64R.
require: **Agency licence and responsible officer:** The IA may approve an individual as responsible officer only if that person is a licensed technical representative (agent), or has applied for that licence. The IA must also be satisfied that the person is fit and proper, and has sufficient authority and resources (s.64ZE(4)).

**Technical representatives (agent):** A person who carries on regulated activities as an agent needs a technical representative (agent) licence, and must be appointed by a licensed agency (s.64Y(1) and (3)). A person may act as agent for only one agency, and only in lines of business that agency is licensed for (s.64L).

**Fit and proper:** The IA must have regard to qualifications, competence, reputation, character and financial standing, among other matters (s.64ZZA(1)). The IA's intermediary fit and proper guideline, GL23, adds detail (reported; check the current text).

**Examinations and continuing education:** The qualifying route runs through the Insurance Intermediaries Qualifying Examination (IIQE). Continuing professional development (CPD) is a condition of renewal under GL24, issued under s.133 (reported; check the current hour requirement).

**Staff restrictions:** A proprietor or partner of the agency, and a director or employee who manages its regulated activities, must not also hold the roles in s.64J(2), such as another agency's agent or a broker company's manager. Breach is an offence (s.64J(3)).

**Notice of appointments and exits:** The agency must notify the IA at least 14 days before appointing a technical representative (agent) (s.64Q(3)). It must notify the IA within 14 days after ending that appointment, or after ending a responsible officer's appointment (s.64R(2) and (4)).

**Responsible officer duties:** The responsible officer must use best endeavours to ensure the agency has proper controls for the conduct requirements in s.90, and that its agents observe them (s.91(2)). The agency must give the officer sufficient authority and resources (s.91(1)(c) and (d)).
gates: **Confirm the licence route:** Decide which entity applies for the agency licence and confirm the route with the IA before the product committee approves the model. Record the answer.

**Name the responsible officer:** Choose a licensed or applicant technical representative (agent) with real authority over insurance sales. Test the choice against s.64ZE(4)(b) and (c) before nomination.

**Map every app role:** List each person who answers product questions, arranges cover or handles claims. Treat each role as needing a licence unless counsel confirms it is clerical or administrative only.

**Check examination and renewal status:** Confirm each licensed person's IIQE route, CPD record and renewal date. Renewal applications must be made no later than 45 days before expiry (s.64ZV(1) and (3)).
**Check group conflicts:** Confirm that no licensed person holds a role with another agency, a broker company or a group entity that s.64J forbids.
**Approve the training plan:** Agree a training plan for front-line staff. The HKMA's Enhanced Competency Framework (ECF) is non-statutory, so use its insurance module as a benchmark (good practice).
watchFor: **Digital journey with no adviser:** A self-service flow can still need licensed staff. If a bank employee answers product questions, arranges cover or helps with a claim, that employee needs the right licence.
**Late notices:** Late notice of an appointment or exit is an offence in its own right, with a fine at level 5 (s.64Q(7) and s.64R(6)). Build the 14-day clock into HR and appointment processes.
**Lapsed licences:** A licence or renewal that lapses while the app keeps selling leaves those sales unlicensed. Track renewal dates across all licensed people.

activities.title: Agency agreements with up to four insurers
activities.summary: An insurance agency signs an agency agreement with each insurer it sells for. The law caps how many insurers an agency may act for, makes the insurer liable for the agent's acts in dealings with clients, and voids any agreement term that cuts back the agent's duty to act in the client's best interests.
activities.route: Yes, as a licensed agency appointed by no more than four insurers, and no more than two of them long-term insurers (Cap. 41K r.3). The agreement must stay within s.68 and must not contract out of the conduct duty in s.90(a) (s.68A).
require: **Appointment cap:** An agency may be appointed for at most four authorized insurers, and no more than two of them may be insurers authorized for long-term business (Cap. 41K r.3). An insurer that knows the agency already holds the maximum must not appoint it, and a breach is an offence with a fine of up to HK$1,000,000 and 2 years' imprisonment on indictment (s.64I(3), (4)(a)).

**Insurer liability:** An insurer is liable for its agent's acts in dealings with clients, even where the act was outside the agent's authority, if the agent is appointed by that insurer alone (s.68(2)). With several insurers, liability depends on which insurers' authority covers the act (s.68(3) to (4B)).

**Authority disclosure:** An insurer is not liable for an act outside its authority if the agent disclosed that fact before the client relied on it, with the clarity and prominence a reasonable client would need (s.68(4C)). The court may still weigh other factors (s.68(4D)).

**Void terms:** A contract or agency agreement term inconsistent with s.68 is void (s.68(4E)). A term that affects the agent's obligation under s.90(a), to act honestly, fairly and in the policy holder's best interests, is void (s.68A).
**Appointment and exit timing:** The insurer must notify the IA at least 14 days before appointing an agency (s.64Q(1)) and within 14 days of terminating it (s.64R(1)).
**Suspension and revocation:** If an agency ceases to be appointed by at least one authorized insurer, its licence is suspended at once, and revoked if the position continues for 180 days (s.64ZH).

**Agent code of conduct:** The IA's Code of Conduct for Licensed Insurance Agents applies to the agency. A breach does not by itself create liability, but it counts in any fit and proper review (s.95(5) and (6)).
gates: **Confirm the insurer panel:** Choose the insurers, within the four-insurer and two-long-term limits, before signing. Record why each insurer was chosen.

**Test each draft against s.68 and s.68A:** Look for terms that cut back the agent's authority, shift liability to the agent, or limit the best-interests duty. Strike or rewrite them, since such terms are void.
**Map the authority scope:** For each insurer and line of business, record what the bank may do. Use the app journeys to test that the authority covers each step.
**Agree the authority disclosure:** Draft the disclosure for acts outside an insurer's authority, and test in the app that it is clear and prominent before a customer relies on the act (s.68(4C)).

**Settle commission and clawback terms:** Put commission, clawback and complaint-split terms in writing. Check they do not create an undisclosed conflict under s.90(f) and (g) (good practice on the commercial terms).
**Secure audit and records rights:** Give the insurer rights to audit sales and complaint records, and keep records that the HKMA can inspect under the s.4G delegation (good practice).
**Plan for exit:** Agree how customers, open policies and data move if an insurer ends its appointment and the panel shrinks.
watchFor: **Thin panel:** Suspension under s.64ZH starts only when no insurer remains. A thin panel carries concentration risk while the licence stays valid.
**Authority drift:** A new product or journey can take the bank outside an insurer's authority. Re-check the authority scope at each launch.

**Agreement terms that cannot be enforced:** Terms void under s.68(4E) or s.68A may still appear in signed agreements. Do not rely on them, and check that the agreement's own terms do not breach s.90(a).

activities.title: Collecting premiums and the IA levy
activities.summary: An agency that collects premium for its insurer handles money that the insurer, not the bank, is owed. The policy holder also pays a prescribed levy to the insurer with each premium, and an intermediary that collects the levy must pass it on promptly. Broker companies face a separate client money regime.
activities.route: Yes, as a licensed agency collecting premium for its appointing insurer, under the agency agreement. The insurer remains liable for the agency's dealings (s.68). The bank must forward any levy it collects to the insurer as soon as practicable (Cap. 41I s.3(2)).
require: **Accounting for premium:** The bank must account for premium promptly and properly (s.90(h)). The agreement should set the remittance cycle and the insurer's audit rights.

**Levy on each premium:** The policy holder owes a prescribed levy to the IA and pays it to the insurer with each premium under a contract of specified general or long term business, other than reinsurance and captive contracts (Cap. 41 s.134(1); Cap. 41I s.3(1); Cap. 41J s.4).

**Levy rate and caps:** From 1 April 2021 the levy is 0.1% of the premium, capped per policy year at HK$5,000 for specified general business and HK$100 for specified long-term business (Cap. 41J ss.4 to 6 and the Schedule). Where premiums are paid more than once a year, the cap applies across the scheduled and extra payments (s.6).

**Intermediary forwarding:** An intermediary, including a licensed insurance intermediary, that collects a levy for the insurer must forward it as soon as practicable (s.3(2) and (7)). The insurer must not keep any excess over the levy (s.3(3)).
**Penalties:** The IA may impose a penalty of up to HK$5,000 on a policy holder who does not pay the levy, and up to HK$10,000 on an insurer that keeps an excess (s.3(4) and (5)).

**Broker money (contrast):** A licensed broker company must hold client monies apart from its own, and pay them into a client account with an authorized institution (s.71(1) and (2); Cap. 41L r.6). These rules apply to broker companies, not to agencies, so check that the bank's flow does not turn it into broker activity.

**Third-party payers and AML:** Where someone other than the policy holder pays the premium, the bank's AML programme should record why, and reflect the customer due diligence and record-keeping requirements in AMLO Schedule 2.
gates: **Map the flow of funds:** Trace each premium from payment to insurer, showing where the levy is held and when it is remitted. Get the insurer's sign-off on the map.
**Build the levy calculation:** Program the 0.1% rate with the per-year caps and the scheduled-payment rule. Test it against the current Schedule to Cap. 41J.
**Agree the remittance cycle:** Set a remittance cycle with the insurer that meets the 'as soon as practicable' standard, and record the levy separately from the premium.
**Confirm no broker activity:** Check that the bank does not hold client monies in a way that makes it a broker company, or that triggers the s.71 and Cap. 41L client account rules.
**Run the AML review:** Confirm the third-party payer rules, source checks and record retention with the AML team, and reflect the outcome in the app flow.

**Agree refunds and cooling-off:** Set how premium is refunded when a policy is cancelled in the cooling-off period. IA guideline GL29 gives 21 calendar days for certain life policies (para 4.2; check the current text). For general cover, check each policy's own cancellation terms.
watchFor: **Levy error:** Charging the levy twice, or keeping it, exposes the insurer to a penalty of up to HK$10,000 (s.3(5)) and strains the agency agreement.
**Multi-payment caps:** Monthly or quarterly plans can exceed the per-year cap if the levy is applied to each payment without the s.6 rule. Test the cap logic on each plan type.
**Premium through an unlicensed route:** A contract made through a person who is not licensed may be enforced or voided at the policy holder's option, with a refund of premium (s.64N(3) and (4)).

activities.title: Sharing customer data with insurers and cross-selling
activities.summary: A bank holds customer data that an insurer needs for underwriting, and may want to use that data to market insurance to its own customers. The PDPO treats both uses as consent questions, and passing data to an insurer for its own marketing needs written consent and specified notices.
activities.route: Yes, but only with the right notices and consent. Sharing application data with the insurer for underwriting and policy administration must fit the collection notice and purpose rules (DPP1 and DPP3). Marketing insurance to the bank's customers, or passing data to an insurer for its marketing, needs the consent steps in ss.35C to 35K.
require: **Collection notice (DPP1):** At collection, the bank must tell the customer the purposes and the classes of persons the data may go to, including insurers. The notice must be explicit where the data subject supplies the data (Sch. 1, DPP1(3)).

**New purpose (DPP3):** Using data for a new purpose needs the data subject's prescribed consent (Sch. 1, DPP3(1)). Test each use, such as insurance cross-selling, against the purpose in the original notice.

**Bank's own direct marketing (ss.35C and 35E):** Before the bank uses personal data to promote insurance, it must give the notice in s.35C and then get consent through a channel it provides free of charge. Consent must cover the kinds of data and the classes of marketing subjects (s.35E(1)). Oral consent needs written confirmation within 14 days.

**Passing data to an insurer (ss.35J and 35K):** Before providing personal data to an insurer for its direct marketing, the bank must give written notice, state whether the data is provided for gain, and get the customer's written consent (s.35J(1) and (2); s.35K(1)).

**Penalties:** Using data for direct marketing without consent is an offence, with a fine of HK$500,000 and three years' imprisonment on conviction (s.35E(4)). Providing data for gain without the s.35J steps carries a fine of HK$1,000,000 and five years (s.35J(5)(a)).
**Common-law confidentiality:** The bank owes customers a common-law duty of confidentiality, which the PDPO does not replace. Check every data flow against the terms the customer accepted.

**Health data in applications:** Health data given in insurance applications flows to the insurer for underwriting. Keep that flow inside the application notice, and do not reuse it for the bank's marketing without fresh consent (DPP3).
gates: **Review each consent screen:** Map each consent in the app to the PDPO section it relies on. Test the flow in the live app, including the free channel for giving or withdrawing consent.
**Separate the consents:** Keep marketing consent apart from the application consent, so the customer can say no to marketing and still apply (good practice).
**Document the insurer terms:** Put the purposes, data classes, retention, security, and the insurer's own marketing limits into the insurer agreement (good practice).
**Keep a consent record:** Store each consent with its date, scope and channel, so the bank can show compliance with s.35E(1) and the written-confirmation rule.
**Minimise the data shared:** Share only the application fields the insurer needs. Data must be adequate but not excessive for the purpose (DPP1(1)(c)).
**Check the data location:** Confirm where the insurer's systems sit and whether the notices name any transfer outside Hong Kong.
**Set up access requests:** Give customers a named contact for access and correction requests, as DPP1(3)(b)(ii) requires.
watchFor: **Bundled consent:** One tick covering the application, the bank's marketing and the sharing with an insurer does not meet the specific consent standard in ss.35E and 35K. Split the consents.
**Silence as consent:** Section 35A counts an indication of no objection as consent. Do not rely on a silent default for cross-selling. Use an affirmative action (good practice).
**Use before notice:** Using data first and giving the notice later breaks the notice-first sequence in ss.35C(1) and 35J(1).

activities.title: HKMA engagement, governance and product approval
activities.summary: The HKMA inspects and investigates a bank's insurance business under powers the IA delegated to it, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases), and the IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA still licenses and disciplines the bank, but must consult the Monetary Authority before it investigates or acts against the bank.
activities.route: Yes, under HKMA supervision. The HKMA exercises the delegated powers over the bank's insurance business (s.4G), and the IA consults it before any investigation or discipline. Tell the HKMA relationship team before launch and record its feedback, since a prior notification duty is reported for some products.
require: **Delegated supervision:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases). The IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)).

**IA consultation before investigation:** Before the IA directs staff or appoints an investigator on a matter concerning an authorized institution or its agent, it must consult the Monetary Authority (s.64ZZH(2)).

**IA consultation before discipline:** Before the IA uses its s.81 disciplinary powers, or an agreed-action power under s.84(1), against an authorized institution or its agent, it must consult the Monetary Authority (ss.82(4) and 84(4)).
**Procedural safeguards:** Before the IA exercises a s.81 power, it must give the bank a reasonable opportunity to be heard, and must issue written notice with reasons (s.82(1) to (3)).

**IA-HKMA memorandum of understanding:** The HKMA and IA signed a memorandum of understanding on 19 July 2019, covering supervision, complaints and enforcement for insurance activities of authorized institutions. The date and title are confirmed; check the MoU text for its full content.

**Prior notification:** HKMA circulars on selling protection linked plans (8 July 2022 and 30 August 2023) are reported to expect a bank to discuss an ILAS launch with the HKMA beforehand (reported; check both circulars).

**ILAS authorization:** An ILAS offered to the public needs SFC authorization under SFO s.104 (SFO s.103 applies to unauthorized offers). The carve-out in s.103(2)(k) covers only offers intended to be disposed of to professional investors, so it does not reach a retail sale (check the current text).
gates: **Open the HKMA conversation early:** Brief the HKMA relationship team on the model, product shelf, target segment and sales channel. Keep a note of what was said and any feedback.
**Confirm the notification duty:** Check whether the reported ILAS and PLP notification point applies to the planned products. Get the circular text before the product committee meets.
**Check IB-1 against the HKMA original:** Read the current IB-1 text on the HKMA site, record its version and date in the approval paper, and do not rely on the law-firm summary.
**Get board sign-off:** The board, or a committee it delegates to, should approve the insurance business model, risk appetite and product approval process (good practice).
**Run a product-approval committee:** Put each insurance product through a documented approval that records compliance, legal and risk views, and the HKMA feedback (good practice).
**Prepare for inspection:** Assemble the sales, complaint and consent records the HKMA may ask for, and name an owner for responses.
**Map the escalation path:** Agree how an HKMA query or an IA investigation notice goes to the board and to legal within a set time.
watchFor: **Two regulators, one issue:** A single complaint can lead to HKMA inspection and an IA investigation. The IA consults the HKMA before acting, so give both regulators consistent answers.
**Stale summaries:** Law-firm summaries of HKMA circulars and IA guidelines may be out of date. Check the current texts before relying on them.
**Launch before notice:** Launching before the HKMA hears of the model may cause supervisory concern, even where no statute is breached, if the reported notification point applies.

**Premium financing:** Where the bank also finances premiums, the HKMA's 1 April 2022 circular and later circulars apply (reported; check the originals). Keep financing separate from the insurance application.

activities.title: Using an insurer's or insurtech's journey inside the app
activities.summary: A bank may show a partner's insurance journey in its app through a web view, an API or a white-label page. The legal test is who negotiates, arranges, invites, induces or advises. That party needs a licence, and co-branding must not suggest a licensed role the bank does not hold.
activities.route: Yes, but only if the party carrying on each regulated step is licensed. Promoting a product in the app is a regulated act if it invites or induces a customer to buy or to make a material decision (Sch. 1A, Part 1 item 1(b) and (c)), so the bank needs an agency appointment for the steps it takes, or must leave those steps to a licensed insurer or intermediary. An insurer may not accept a referral from an unlicensed person (s.64N(2)).
require: **Who carries on the regulated steps:** Negotiating or arranging a contract, inviting or inducing a person to buy or to make a material decision, and giving regulated advice are all regulated acts (Sch. 1A, Part 1 items 1(a) to (d)). Map each step to a licensed party before design.

**Holding out:** No one may hold out as carrying on regulated activity in the course of business or for reward without a licence (s.64G(2)). An agency may hold out that it acts as agent of the insurer that appointed it (s.64G(3)(a)(ii)), so co-branding that names the appointing insurer and the bank's agency role can fit that exception. A slogan that suggests the bank is the insurer or an unlicensed partner does not.

**No unlicensed referrals:** An insurer must not enter a contract through a person in Hong Kong, or accept a referral from one, unless that person is a licensed agency or individual agent appointed by the insurer, a licensed broker company, or has only clerical or administrative duties (s.64N(1) and (2)).

**Consequence of breach:** A contract made in breach of s.64N(1) can be enforced or voided at the policy holder's option, and a policy holder who voids it can recover the consideration paid (s.64N(3) and (4)).

**Arranging is wider than negotiating:** Under the IA's explanatory note on regulated activities, a party is arranging where its conduct brings the contract into effect, for example by helping a customer apply and passing the application to the insurer (reported; check the current text).

**Bank referrals:** The IA's 2019 explanatory note for banks, prepared with the HKMA and the Hong Kong Association of Banks, treats a referral as regulated activity where the bank steers a client toward a specific intermediary's product, or earns direct pay for it.
**Outsourcing and technology risk:** The bank's HKMA outsourcing and technology-risk obligations, including SPM modules SA-2 and TM-G-1, should be checked against the partner journey.
gates: **Map each step to a licensed party:** For every screen, record who negotiates, arranges, invites or induces, advises, and collects premium. Confirm each of those parties holds the right licence.
**Choose the model:** Decide between a bank-run agency journey, a web view hosted by a licensed insurer, or an insurtech partner's journey. Record why each one is lawful for this bank.
**Approve co-branding copy:** Review logos, slogans and banners against the holding-out rule before launch. Avoid wording that suggests the bank is the insurer or a licensed partner.
**Confirm the appointment scope:** Confirm the insurer is authorized, and that any bank appointment covers each line of business in the journey (s.64G(3)).
**Contract the outsourcing:** Include audit, data, security, continuity and exit terms with the partner, consistent with the bank's SA-2 and TM-G-1 framework.
**Test the insurer's cyber controls:** Ask the insurer for evidence it meets GL20, including its 72-hour incident notice to the IA (reported).
**Check the web-view data flow:** Confirm which party collects and holds customer data in the journey, and that the consent flow for data sharing covers it.
watchFor: **Hidden regulated steps:** A partner's journey may quote or advise on screens the bank never designed. Review the whole flow end to end, not only the partner's brochure.
**Fee-linked referrals:** Paying the bank for each sale or referral may turn the arrangement into regulated arranging, while a flat fee is less likely to do so. Structure any fee with counsel.
**Partner licence lapses:** If the partner's licence or appointment ends, the journey must close at once, or the bank keeps selling through an unlicensed route.

title: Selling insurance in the app
oneLiner: The app can sell insurance only through a licensed route, and each product family adds its own rules on needs, disclosure and cooling-off.
keyPoints: **Licensed channel:** s.64N(1) lets an authorized insurer contract through another person in Hong Kong only if that person is a licensed agency, a licensed individual insurance agent appointed by the insurer, a licensed broker company, or has clerical duties only.

**Product families:** Sch. 1 sorts business into long term classes (Pt 2) and general classes (Pt 3). Para 3A stops retirement-scheme classes G and H from being combined with other business, subject to exemptions.
**Conduct duties:** s.90 applies whenever the intermediary carries on a [[regulated activity|Regulated activity]]. The duties cover best interests, care, needs, disclosure and conflicts.
**Wide scope:** Sch. 1A, Pt 1 treats inviting or inducing a person to buy as a regulated activity. Promotions in the app therefore count, not only the sale itself.

**Cooling-off:** IA guideline GL29 gives 21 calendar days to cancel for a premium refund on certain life policies (para 4.2 lists them; check the current text). It is a guideline under s.133, not law in itself. For general cover, check each policy's own cancellation terms.

**Premium and levy:** The policy holder owes the levy to the IA (Cap. 41 s.134(1)) and pays it to the insurer with each premium (Cap. 41I s.3(1)); the insurer remits it to the IA (Cap. 41I s.4). The app's premium flow must carry the levy with each payment.

points: **General classes:** Short-term cover is the simplest starting point, but the same conduct duties in s.90 still apply.
**Long term protection:** Life and permanent health cover sit in Sch. 1, Pt 2. Long-term sales add needs analysis and illustration duties.

**VHIS:** The Health Bureau, not the Insurance Authority, certifies Voluntary Health Insurance Scheme plans. Only certified plans qualify for the tax deduction, so the app must show certification clearly.
**QDAP:** The Insurance Authority certifies Qualifying Deferred Annuity Policies. Only certified products qualify for the deduction, and only premiums due and paid in the year of assessment count.
**ILAS:** Investment-linked products need SFC authorization under SFO s.104 and must meet the ILAS Code. Treat them as a separate authorization track.
deepDive.takeaway: Map each product to its class and any certification before build starts, because the class sets the rules the app must follow.

points: **Product information:** Show key facts before the customer applies. Once the app invites a purchase, the content is a conduct matter.

**Needs analysis:** GL30, the IA's Guideline on Financial Needs Analysis, asks intermediaries to carry out a needs analysis before recommending a policy. Its Interpretation Notes are reported to say they do not have the force of law.
**Disclosure:** s.90(e) requires disclosure needed for an informed decision. s.90(f) and (g) require conflicts to be avoided where possible and disclosed where they remain.

**Application and signature:** An electronic signature meets a signing requirement only if the method is reliable for its purpose and the other party consents to it (ETO s.6(1)). ETO s.17 says an electronic contract is not denied effect solely because it is electronic.

**Cooling-off:** For certain life policies, GL29 gives 21 calendar days from delivery of the policy or a cooling-off notice, whichever is earlier, with a premium refund (para 4.2; check the current text). The app must record the delivery date.
deepDive.takeaway: Each step produces evidence, so design the records before the screens.

deepDive.heading: Advised and execution-only sales
deepDive.lede: The label non-advised does not remove conduct duties from an agency.
points: **Scope of s.90:** s.90 applies whenever the intermediary carries on a regulated activity. It does not depend on whether the customer asked for advice.

**Regulated advice:** Sch. 1A, Pt 3 treats giving an opinion on a matter such as an application, a change or a claim as [[regulated advice|Regulated advice]]. An app that recommends a product is giving advice, whatever it is called.
**Competence:** s.90(c) allows advice only on matters the intermediary is competent to advise. A comparison or best-for-you feature must be built to that limit.
**Online guidance:** An IA guideline on insurance activities over the internet, listed as GL8, should be read before any execution-only design. Check its current title and text.
deepDive.takeaway: Decide the advice position for each screen before launch, and assume s.90 applies to all of them.

deepDive.heading: Special customers
deepDive.lede: Some customers need extra care, and the rules for them are thinner than the rules for others.
points: **Elderly and vulnerable customers:** No IA or HKMA rule specific to these customers is known; check the current text. Work through s.90(d), which asks the intermediary to consider the customer's circumstances, and through the needs analysis.

**Non-residents:** s.64H treats active marketing to the public from outside Hong Kong as holding out as carrying on a regulated activity, whether the marketing is done by the person or for it. An app marketed to overseas customers needs review.
**Mainland visitors:** A 2016 IA circular is reported to require an Important Facts Statement for new long-term applications from mainland visitors (reported; check the current requirement).
**Minors:** Sales to minors are not covered here. Treat any app sale to a minor as a separate question and take advice before offering it.
deepDive.takeaway: Set an eligibility rule in the app for each product, and log why a customer was accepted or declined.

deepDive.heading: Premium financing and tie-ins
deepDive.lede: Loans linked to insurance are where bank and insurer duties most often overlap.
points: **Premium financing:** HKMA circular announced by press release on 1 April 2022 (see stage 8) sets standards for [[premium financing|Premium financing]] used to buy life policies, applying from 1 January 2023. Affordability should be tested, not assumed.

**Separation:** A reported HKMA circular of 19 November 2025 stresses separating financing from insurance applications and prohibits return-enhancing promotions. Confidence is low, so check the HKMA original.
**Tied selling:** Check the current Code of Banking Practice text for tied-selling rules before designing any loan or insurance tie-in.
**Mortgage-linked cover:** Fire and life cover tied to a mortgage needs review for tying and conduct rules. Agree the standard wording with counsel.
deepDive.takeaway: Keep the loan decision and the insurance decision on separate screens, each with its own consent.

deepDive.heading: Marketing and promotions
deepDive.lede: An app banner that invites a purchase is a regulated activity, so marketing is a conduct question as well as a privacy one.

visual.caption: A banner can trigger both the conduct rules and the marketing consent rules.
