deepDive.heading: Authorization
deepDive.lede: The IA authorizes insurers company by company and class by class.
points: **Application:** A company applies in writing under s.7, in the specified form and with the information the IA requires.
**Grant:** The IA may authorize the company for a class of business, subject to conditions, under s.8 or s.8A.
**Mandatory refusal:** The IA must refuse if a director or controller is not fit and proper, or if the capital and reinsurance tests in s.8(3) are not met.
**Conditions:** The IA may amend or revoke conditions, or impose new ones, by notice (s.12). It may then direct that the register is updated.
**Special purpose insurers:** Under s.8A, the company needs at least two fit and proper directors, a fit and proper administrator as controller, and must carry on special purpose business only.
deepDive.takeaway: Start every partner review with the register entry and the conditions attached to it.

deepDive.heading: Fit and proper people and controllers
deepDive.lede: The IA vets the people who run and own the insurer, not only the company itself.
points: **Controllers:** Under s.9, a controller includes a managing director, a chief executive, a person whose directions the board follows, or a person entitled to 15% or more of the votes. The insurer needs IA approval before appointing one (s.13A).

**Directors:** An HK insurer must obtain IA approval before appointing a director (s.13AC). The IA may later revoke the approval if the person ceases to be fit and proper. The insurer must then end the appointment by the date the notice sets (s.13AC(8)).
**Key persons:** A non-captive authorized insurer needs IA approval before appointing a key person in control functions (s.13AE).
**Shareholders:** A person who becomes a minority or majority shareholder controller needs IA approval under s.13B. A bank group taking a stake may trigger this.
**Fit and proper test:** The IA weighs competence, honesty, financial standing, any disciplinary history with the HKMA or SFC, group information and internal controls (s.14A(1)).
deepDive.takeaway: Ask the insurer for evidence of IA approval for each person who will deal with the bank.

deepDive.heading: Capital and valuation
deepDive.lede: Capital and fund rules decide whether the insurer can keep writing business.
points: **Continuing compliance:** An authorized insurer must keep its capital requirements met at all times and make the reports the IA prescribes (s.13AA(1)-(3)). A breach is an offence (s.13AA(4)).
**Risk-based capital:** The risk-based capital (RBC) regime took effect on 1 July 2024. Detailed quantitative rules are reported to sit in the Insurance (Valuation and Capital) Rules (Cap. 41R).

**Proposed changes:** Reports say the IA consulted in February 2026 on refinements to Cap. 41R, with conclusions published in May 2026 and implementation targeted for 31 December 2026. Check the current status.
**Separate funds:** Part IV requires separate accounts and funds for long term business (s.21B). Part IVA does the same for general business (s.25AA).

**Assets in Hong Kong:** Part IVA requires general business insurers to hold assets in Hong Kong against onshore liabilities, in at least the amount the rules prescribe (s.25A(3)). Sch. 8 lists the qualifying assets.
deepDive.takeaway: Ask for the insurer's latest capital position and confirm how its funds are held.

deepDive.heading: Supervision and intervention
deepDive.lede: The IA can act at several levels, from restricting new business to withdrawing authorization.
points: **Powers of intervention:** Part V lets the IA restrict new business (s.27), set requirements on investments (s.28) and assets (s.29), and impose further requirements (s.35).
**Further powers:** Part VA covers inspections, investigations and disciplinary action against authorized insurers (s.41P), with procedural rules in s.41Q.
**Group supervision:** Part XIA covers designated insurance holding companies and their supervised groups, including approvals at group level.

**Digital insurers:** The IA launched Fast Track on 29 September 2017 for insurers selling only through digital channels. An official speech in December 2025 said four digital insurers had been authorized under it.
**Bank implication:** A restriction can stop sales in the app at short notice. The agency agreement should let the bank pause or switch products quickly.
deepDive.takeaway: Agree in advance how sales pause if the insurer comes under an IA restriction.

deepDive.heading: Partner due diligence
deepDive.lede: A diligence file should show that the insurer will stand behind its agents and its products.
points: **Register check:** Confirm the insurer is on the IA register for the classes the bank will sell (s.5H), and that no condition restricts them.
**Approvals:** Ask for evidence of IA approval for the controllers, directors and key persons who will sign the partnership or supervise it (ss.13A, 13AC, 13AE).
**Agency oversight:** Ask how the insurer monitors its agents' sales conduct and complaints, and what sales records it can see.

**Disclosure:** Check whether the Insurance (Public Disclosure) Rules (Cap. 41W) apply to the insurer and what they require. The rules are reported to have come into operation on 22 May 2026 (IA public disclosure page, https://www.ia.org.hk/en/consumer/public_disclosure_of_the_insurers.html). Check the current text.

**Agency agreement:** The IA has required insurers to appoint agents under a standalone written agreement meeting the Hong Kong Federation of Insurers' model minimum terms (IA circular, 2010). Check the current requirements before relying on it.

**Class authorization:** Confirm the insurer is authorized for each class the bank will sell. Writing a class without authorization is an offence (s.6), and the contract may be void at the policy holder's option (s.6A).
deepDive.takeaway: Diligence the insurer's control environment before the product, not after launch.

provisions.title: Authorization: long term business and general business
provisions.summary: A company applies in writing to the IA. The IA may authorize a class of business, subject to conditions, but must refuse if a director or controller is not fit and proper, or if any condition in s.8(3) is not met, such as the capital, reinsurance or name tests.
provisions.counselNote: Ask for the insurer's authorized classes and conditions. An authorization for one class does not cover another, so check each product line.

provisions.title: Register of authorized insurers
provisions.summary: The IA keeps a register of each authorized insurer, its classes and restricting conditions, and makes it available for inspection online as far as practicable.
provisions.counselNote: Check the register at onboarding and again before each product launch. Keep a dated copy for the file.

provisions.title: Meaning of controller
provisions.summary: A controller includes a managing director, a chief executive, a person whose directions the directors are accustomed to follow, or a person entitled to 15% or more of the voting power.
provisions.counselNote: Map the controllers of any insurer the bank considers, including shareholders in its group, before negotiating.

provisions.title: Approval of certain controllers of authorized insurers
provisions.summary: An authorized insurer must not appoint a controller unless the IA has approved the appointment. The IA may approve only if satisfied the individual is fit and proper.
provisions.counselNote: Ask for the approval for each controller. A bank group that appoints its own executive as a controller of an insurer needs the same approval.

provisions.title: Approval of directors of HK insurers or designated insurers
provisions.summary: An HK insurer or designated insurer must not appoint a director without IA approval. The IA can revoke approval later if the person is no longer fit and proper.
provisions.counselNote: Track board changes at the insurer. Revocation is possible after appointment, so the bank should not assume a director is approved for life.

provisions.title: Approval of key persons in control functions of certain authorized insurers
provisions.summary: A non-captive authorized insurer must not appoint a key person in control functions unless the IA has approved the appointment, and the IA must be satisfied the person is fit and proper.
provisions.counselNote: Identify the insurer's approved key persons early and confirm who signs off the bank's product and conduct controls.

provisions.title: Contracts of insurance made through persons other than licensed insurance intermediaries, etc.
provisions.summary: An authorized insurer must not contract through, or accept a referral from, a person in Hong Kong unless that person is a licensed agency or licensed individual agent appointed by the insurer, a licensed broker company, or performs only clerical or administrative duties. Breach is an offence (s.64N(5)). For a contract made through an unlicensed person in breach of s.64N(1), the policy holder may enforce it or treat it as void (s.64N(3)).
provisions.counselNote: The bank may sell or refer only through the routes s.64N allows. An unlicensed or unappointed bank puts both the insurer and the contract at risk.

provisions.title: Authorized insurer's relationship with its agent
provisions.summary: An insurer that appoints an agent is liable for the agent's acts in dealings with clients, even outside the agent's authority. Liability falls on the insurer alone, or jointly where several insurers appoint the agent. An insurer escapes liability for an act outside the agent's authority only if the agent disclosed that lack of authority, with the clarity and prominence a client reasonably needs, before the client relied on it. The court may weigh other factors (s.68(4C)-(4D)).
provisions.counselNote: Set out in the agency agreement who handles sales conduct, complaints and training, and how the insurer will see the bank's sales records.

provisions.title: Powers of Intervention
provisions.summary: Lets the IA restrict new business, set requirements on investments and assets, impose directions, appoint a manager in some cases, and, through a direction under s.40, end authorization for business the insurer has stopped writing. Revocation for misconduct is in Part VA (s.41P).
provisions.counselNote: Prepare a playbook for a restriction: how sales pause, how customers and the register are informed, and who decides.

provisions.title: Insurance Groups and Insurance Holding Companies
provisions.summary: Covers designation of insurance holding companies, their supervised groups, and shareholder and director approvals at group level. Its provisions parallel the controller approvals in Part I of the Ordinance.
provisions.counselNote: If a bank group holds an insurer through a holding company, check early whether that company is or could be designated.

provisions.title: Insurance (Valuation and Capital) Rules
provisions.summary: Set the detailed risk-based capital rules for insurers, in force from 1 July 2024 alongside the Insurance (Amendment) Ordinance 2023. The IA has consulted on refinements in 2026. Check the current text.
provisions.counselNote: Ask for the insurer's RBC position and confirm the current version of the rules before relying on any figure.

provisions.instrument: Insurance (Maximum Number of Authorized Insurers) Rules
provisions.title: Maximum number of authorized insurers
provisions.summary: A licensed person may be appointed as an agent for at most four authorized insurers, of which no more than two may write long term business. Rule 5 counts appointments by insurers in the same group in a way that can reduce the number counted.
provisions.counselNote: Count the bank's appointments for each line of business before signing with a second insurer, and check whether a group partner counts as one.

checklist: **Check the register:** Confirm the insurer's name, authorized classes and restricting conditions on the IA register (s.5H).
**Ask for approvals:** Obtain evidence of IA approval for each controller, director and key person who will deal with the bank (ss.13A, 13AC, 13AE).
**Verify the agency route:** Confirm the bank's licence or appointment status fits s.64N before any contract is signed.
**Count the appointments:** Apply Cap. 41K, r.3 and r.5 to the bank's list of appointed insurers, including group partners.
**Review capital:** Request the insurer's RBC position and confirm the current version of Cap. 41R.
**Agree the agency terms:** Allocate sales conduct, complaints and training duties in the agency agreement, reflecting the insurer's liability under s.68.
**Plan for restrictions:** Agree how sales pause if the IA restricts new business under Part V.
**Map group links:** Identify shareholder controllers and any holding company, and their approvals under s.13B and Part XIA.
itAngle: **Partner data:** The register, approvals and conditions change over time. Keep a dated record and set a monitoring alert for changes.
**Agent feeds:** Insurer systems for appointments must link to the bank's sales journey, so that only products the insurer has authorized the bank to sell can be shown.
**Restriction switch:** A Part V restriction may need a product-level switch in the app. Build and test it before it is needed.
**Evidence:** Keep proof of approvals and register checks in a form the IA can inspect on request.
bankNotes: **Agency route:** To sell an insurer's product, the bank must be a licensed insurance agency appointed by that insurer (s.64N(1)(a)(i)), or a licensed broker company (s.64N(1)(a)(ii)). Stage 6 covers the bank's licensing.

**Group insurers:** Where the bank group owns an insurer, Cap. 41K, r.5 may reduce the number of insurers counted against the four-insurer limit. Confirm the count for each line before adding a partner.

**Acquiring an insurer:** A bank group that becomes a shareholder controller of an insurer, through a minority or majority stake, needs IA approval (s.13B). A 15% voting-power stake is enough to be a controller (s.9). A designated holding company brings Part XIA approvals.
**Sister insurers:** Selling a group insurer's products creates conflicts that the conduct rules must address. Disclose the group link to customers and record why the product was chosen.
pitfalls: **Unlicensed selling:** Taking an insurer's business through an unlicensed bank exposes the insurer to an offence and the contract to avoidance (s.64N(3)-(5)).
**Marketing over register:** Relying on a partner's marketing claims without checking the IA register and conditions.
**Approvals assumed:** Assuming a group's approvals carry over to a new controller or director. Each appointment needs its own approval (ss.13A, 13AC).
**Stale capital data:** Relying on last year's capital figures when the RBC regime and its refinements change the numbers.

glossary.definition: A company authorized under s.8 or s.8A to carry on insurance business. Only authorized insurers may write insurance business in or from Hong Kong, subject to limited exceptions.
Under s.9, a managing director, a chief executive, a person whose directions the board follows, or a person entitled to 15% or more of the votes. Some controllers need IA approval before appointment.
A person who becomes a controller through a shareholding, as a minority or majority holder. The change needs IA approval under s.13B.
An individual appointed to a control function of a non-captive authorized insurer. The appointment needs IA approval under s.13AE.
An insurer authorized only for special purpose business under s.8A. It must have at least two fit and proper directors and a fit and proper administrator as controller.
The capital regime for insurers in force from 1 July 2024. Its detailed rules are in the Insurance (Valuation and Capital) Rules (Cap. 41R).
A holding company of an insurance group that the IA designates under Part XIA. Its supervised group is subject to group-level supervision.
The IA's route for applicants that will sell only through digital channels. It was launched on 29 September 2017.

A business licensed under Cap. 41 to carry on regulated activities as agent of one or more authorized insurers that appointed it (s.64G(3)(a), s.64U(1), (5)(b)). Under s.64N, an insurer may contract only through its own appointed agencies or agents, a licensed broker company, or a person doing clerical or administrative work.

title: Licensing the bank and its people
oneLiner: A bank that sells insurance needs licensed entities, licensed staff and an approved responsible officer, all kept valid and up to date.
keyPoints: **Two layers of licence:** The bank holds an insurance agency or broker company licence. Its staff hold technical representative licences. Cap. 41 sets out the five licence types in s.64F.
**Validity:** Agency, TR (agent), broker company and TR (broker) licences each run for three years from grant, unless the Insurance Authority (IA) sets another period (ss.64V, 64Z, 64ZB, 64ZD).
**[[Responsible officer]]:** Every agency needs an IA-approved responsible officer who is a licensed TR (agent), or an applicant for that licence (s.64ZE(4)(a)).

**Limits on appointments:** A TR (agent) may act for only one agency at a time (s.64L(1)). An agency may be appointed by at most four insurers, no more than two of them for long term business (s.64I(1); Cap. 41K, r.3).

**Notice duties:** New TR appointments need 14 days' prior notice (s.64Q(3)). Leavers and changes in particulars need notice within 14 days (ss.64R, 64P(3)). Changes in directors or controllers need notice within one month (s.64ZZD(1)).

**HKMA role:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the [[Monetary Authority]], a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases). The IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)), and must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)).

deepDive.heading: The five licences and the bank's route
deepDive.lede: A bank usually enters as a licensed agency, with its staff licensed as technical representatives.
points: **Agency licence (s.64U):** Granted to a sole proprietor, partnership or company, to act as agent of an authorized insurer in one or more lines of business (s.64U(1), (4)).
**Appointment first:** The applicant must be appointed as an agent by at least one authorized insurer (s.64U(5)(b)).
**No dual licence:** An applicant for an agency licence must not hold, or be applying for, an individual agent, TR (agent), broker company or TR (broker) licence (s.64U(5)(c)).

**Accompanying applications:** The agency application must come with either a TR (agent) application and a responsible officer application, or a responsible officer approval for a licensed TR (s.64U(3)). The IA grants or rejects these together (s.64U(6), (7)).

**Broker route (ss.64ZA, 64ZC):** A broker company acts as agent of the policy holder, not the insurer (s.64G(3)(d)). Its staff hold TR (broker) licences, and its responsible officers are approved under s.64ZF.
deepDive.takeaway: For a bank that sells insurers' products, the agency route is the natural fit. The broker route applies only if the bank will act for customers.

deepDive.heading: Responsible officers
deepDive.lede: The responsible officer is the person the IA holds accountable for conduct controls within the agency.
points: **Who qualifies:** The officer must be a licensed TR (agent), or an applicant for one (s.64ZE(4)(a)). Each TR (agent) must also be appointed by the agency (s.64Y(3)(b)).

**Approval test:** The IA must be satisfied the officer will be fit and proper, alone or with other officers, and has sufficient authority from the agency and sufficient resources and support (s.64ZE(4)(b), (c)). The same test applies to broker company officers under s.64ZF(4).

**Agency duties:** The agency must give its responsible officer sufficient authority and resources (s.91(1)(c), (d)) and maintain controls for compliance with the conduct requirements in s.90 (s.91(1)(a)).
**Officer duties:** The responsible officer must use best endeavours to make sure the agency has those controls and that its TR (agent)s observe them (s.91(2)).

**Without an officer:** If the agency loses its responsible officer, the IA may suspend the licence after notice and an opportunity to make representations (s.64ZN(1), (3)). It may revoke the licence if no replacement is applied for within 90 days of suspension, or if the application is rejected (s.64ZN(2)).
deepDive.takeaway: Name a second licensed TR (agent) as back-up, because losing the officer can suspend the whole agency licence.

deepDive.heading: Limits on personnel and appointments
deepDive.lede: The Ordinance restricts how many insurers an agency can serve and how individuals can be shared between firms.
points: **Insurer limit:** An agency must not be appointed for more than the prescribed number of insurers (s.64I(1)). Cap. 41K, r.3 sets that at four, of which no more than two may be insurers authorized for long term business (text dated 19 March 2020).

**Insurer side:** An insurer that knows the agency is already at the limit must not appoint it (s.64I(3)). Breach can bring a fine of $1,000,000 and two years' imprisonment on indictment (s.64I(4)(a)).

**Dual roles:** A proprietor, partner, or a director or employee who manages regulated activities cannot also be a partner or proprietor of another agency, an individual agent, a TR (agent) of another agency, a TR (broker), or a manager at another agency or broker company (s.64J(2)).
**One agency per TR:** A TR (agent) must not be licensed for a second agency (s.64L(1)). The TR may sell only lines of business that the appointing agency is licensed for (s.64L(2)).

**Notice:** A TR (agent) appointment needs 14 days' prior notice (s.64Q(3)). A termination of a TR or responsible officer needs notice within 14 days (s.64R(2), (4)). Changes in name, address, phone or email need notice within 14 days (s.64P(3)).
deepDive.takeaway: Keep an appointments calendar: 14 days before a new TR starts, and 14 days after a leaver goes.

deepDive.heading: Fit and proper and competence
deepDive.lede: Fitness and propriety is the main test for every licence and every officer, and the IA also expects training.
points: **Statutory test:** The IA weighs qualifications and experience, the ability to act competently, honestly and fairly, reputation, integrity, financial standing, and past discipline by the Monetary Authority, SFC, MPFA or similar bodies (s.64ZZA(1)(a)-(e)).
**Wider view for agencies:** For agency and broker company applications and renewals, the IA also considers related persons and the firm's internal controls and risk management (s.64ZZA(2)).
**IA guideline:** The IA's fit and proper guideline for intermediaries (GL23, reported) applies the statutory test in more detail. Check the current text.

**Examinations:** The IA's application notes (reported) tie licensing to IIQE papers. The reported pass mark is 70%, and results are not accepted after two consecutive years without insurance work in Hong Kong.
**Continuing development:** Continuing professional development under GL24 is a condition of renewal while the individual remains licensed (reported). Check the current annual hour requirement.
deepDive.takeaway: Build one training matrix covering IIQE status, CPD hours and the HKMA's ECF modules, and check each requirement against the current source.

deepDive.heading: Keeping the licence valid
deepDive.lede: A licence lasts three years, and most of the work is in renewals and notices.
points: **Validity:** Each licence is valid for three years from grant, or another period the IA sets (ss.64V, 64Z, 64ZB, 64ZD).
**Renewal:** The application may be made no later than 45 days before expiry (s.64ZV(3)). The IA may renew on payment of the prescribed fee (s.64ZV(4)).
**Agency renewal test:** The IA must be satisfied that the agency's legal form has not changed since the first application, and that it remains fit and proper (s.64ZV(5)(a), (b)).
**Officer at renewal:** The IA must also be satisfied that the agency has a responsible officer, or has applied for one under s.64ZE (s.64ZV(5)(d)).
**Conditions:** The IA may impose, change or revoke conditions on a licence or officer approval by written notice (s.64ZG(2)-(5)).

**False information:** Making a false or misleading statement in a licence or approval application, knowingly or recklessly, is an offence. So is omitting a material particular. The penalty is a level 5 fine and six months' imprisonment (s.64ZZE(1)-(3)).
deepDive.takeaway: Diarise renewal 45 days before expiry, and treat every notice period as a hard deadline.

deepDive.heading: Lines of business
deepDive.lede: A licence covers only the lines of business written into it, and changing them needs IA approval.
points: **Scope:** An agency licence covers one or more lines of business specified in it (s.64U(4)). A TR (agent) licence is limited in the same way (s.64Y(2)).

**Variation:** A licensed intermediary may apply to vary its lines of business (s.64S(1)). The IA must be satisfied the applicant remains fit and proper after the change (s.64S(4)), and must update the register (s.64S(7)).
**Individuals follow the agency:** A TR (agent) must not sell in a line of business unless the appointing agency is also licensed for it (s.64L(2)).

**Long term and general classes:** The Ordinance refers to long term business for insurer limits (Cap. 41K, r.3). The class definitions should be checked against the current text before a licence application.
deepDive.takeaway: Before a new product line goes live, check that the agency and the TR are both licensed for it, and that the insurer is authorized for that class.

provisions.title: Interpretation of Part X
provisions.summary: Defines the five licence types (agency, individual agent, TR (agent), broker company, TR (broker)), the controller test of 15% or more of capital, profits or votes, and the agency agreement. Each licence type is tied to its grant section.
provisions.counselNote: Start every licensing analysis here. The bank needs an agency or broker licence and TR licences for its staff, and each must be matched to a grant section.

provisions.title: Grant of licence: insurance agency
provisions.summary: An agency licence is granted to a sole proprietor, partnership or company acting as agent of an authorized insurer. It must be applied for with a TR (agent) application and responsible officer application, or with a responsible officer approval for a licensed TR. The applicant must be fit and proper and appointed by at least one insurer.
provisions.counselNote: The bank files the agency application with its first responsible officer. Check that the insurer appointment is in place before filing, since s.64U(5)(b) makes it a condition.

provisions.title: Validity of insurance agency licence
provisions.summary: A licence granted under s.64U is valid for three years from grant, or another period the IA sets. Sections 64Z, 64ZB and 64ZD apply the same three-year rule to TR (agent), broker company and TR (broker) licences.
provisions.counselNote: Keep a single register of expiry dates for the bank and every TR. Expiry without renewal means the licence lapses, and the sales channel stops.

provisions.title: Grant of licence: technical representative (agent)
provisions.summary: An individual may apply for a TR (agent) licence to act as agent of a licensed agency. The IA must be satisfied the applicant is fit and proper, appointed by a licensed agency or an applicant agency, and holds no other agency-type licence.
provisions.counselNote: Bank staff who sell insurance need this licence whatever their HKMA registration. The appointment must come from the bank's agency, so sequence the appointment with the application.

provisions.title: Approval of responsible officers of licensed insurance agencies
provisions.summary: A licensed agency, or an applicant, may ask the IA to approve an individual as responsible officer. The IA must be satisfied the individual is a licensed or applicant TR (agent), is fit and proper, and has sufficient authority, resources and support. Refusals must give reasons.
provisions.counselNote: The responsible officer's approval is the bank's most visible compliance control. Build the file around the three limbs of s.64ZE(4)(b) and (c): fitness, authority and resources.

provisions.title: Restrictions in relation to number of authorized insurers of each licensed insurance agency, etc.
provisions.summary: An agency must not be appointed for more than the prescribed maximum number of insurers. An insurer that knows the agency is at that limit must not appoint it. Breaches are offences, with a level 6 fine for the agency and a $1,000,000 fine and two years' imprisonment on indictment for the insurer.
provisions.counselNote: Before onboarding a new insurer, check the bank's existing appointments. The offence sits with both sides, so the insurer will also ask the question.

provisions.instrument: Insurance (Maximum Number of Authorized Insurers) Rules (Cap. 41K)
provisions.title: Maximum number of authorized insurers
provisions.summary: A person may be appointed as a licensed person for a maximum of four authorized insurers, of which no more than two may be insurers authorized for long term business. The text is dated 19 March 2020.
provisions.counselNote: The text is dated 19 March 2020. Confirm the current number on the Cap. 41K amendment history and with the IA before planning a multi-insurer product shelf. Insurers in the same group count as one general and one long term insurer, or as one insurer if every appointment is limited to one line of business (Cap. 41K, r.5).

provisions.title: Restrictions in relation to personnel of licensed insurance agencies
provisions.summary: Owners, partners, directors and employees who manage regulated activities of an agency must not also hold roles with another agency or broker company, or be individual agents or TR (broker)s. A breach is an offence carrying a level 6 fine and six months' imprisonment.
provisions.counselNote: Check secondary jobs and group roles of senior bank staff who manage insurance sales, since these can breach s.64J even when no licence changes.

provisions.title: Duty to notify Authority of appointment
provisions.summary: An insurer or licensed intermediary must notify the IA in writing at least 14 days before appointing an agency, individual agent, or TR (agent) or TR (broker). The notice must include a fee and the prescribed particulars. The IA updates the register unless it has concerns about compliance.
provisions.counselNote: Set a 14-day lead time in the onboarding plan for every new TR. A late notice is an offence under s.64Q(7).

provisions.title: Determination of fit and proper
provisions.summary: Sets the matters the IA must consider when deciding whether a person is fit and proper. These cover qualifications, competence, reputation, financial standing, past discipline by financial regulators, group information, and other business activities. For agencies and broker companies, related persons and internal controls also count.
provisions.counselNote: Prepare a fit and proper file for each officer and TR before filing, covering the seven matters in s.64ZZA(1), including any past regulatory history.

provisions.title: Renewal of licences
provisions.summary: A licensee may apply to renew, but no later than 45 days before expiry. For agencies, the IA must be satisfied the legal form has not changed since the first application, and that the applicant remains fit and proper.
provisions.counselNote: Diarise renewal filings at least 45 days early, and check that the legal form of the agency has not changed since the original application.

provisions.title: Conduct requirements for licensed insurance agencies and their responsible officers
provisions.summary: The agency must maintain controls to secure compliance with the conduct requirements in s.90 by itself and its TR (agent)s, and use best endeavours to secure observance. Its responsible officer must give sufficient authority and resources, and use best endeavours to ensure those controls exist and are observed.
provisions.counselNote: The conduct controls sit with the agency and the officer, not only the sales staff. Map each control in the conduct stage to a named owner.

checklist: **Confirm the entity route:** Decide whether the bank will be a licensed insurance agency, a broker company, or both, and record the reasoning against ss.64U and 64ZA.
**Name the first responsible officer:** Identify a bank TR (agent) who can be approved under s.64ZE, and check the fit and proper file before filing.
**Secure insurer appointments first:** Obtain at least one insurer appointment before filing, as s.64U(5)(b) requires, and check the four-insurer limit under Cap. 41K, r.3.
**Plan TR licensing for every seller:** Map each staff member who will sell insurance to a TR (agent) application, the IIQE papers for the relevant lines, and an appointment under s.64Y(3)(b).
**Run a 14-day notice calendar:** Set up a workflow for s.64Q appointments, s.64R terminations and s.64P changes, with named owners.
**Diarise renewals and officer succession:** Record every expiry, set renewal reminders 45 days before expiry under s.64ZV(3), and keep a back-up responsible officer.
**Check dual roles:** Review senior staff's other roles against s.64J(2) before appointing them to manage insurance sales.
**Keep the public register accurate:** Compare the bank's details with the IA register each quarter, since the IA keeps that register under s.64O.
itAngle: **Licence register as system of record:** Hold each licence, its expiry date, its conditions and its appointing insurer in one table. Link it to the staff HR system so that a leaver triggers the s.64R notice.
**Automated expiry alerts:** Set alerts at 90, 60 and 45 days before each expiry, with the last alert tied to the s.64ZV(3) deadline.

**Access control on sales tools:** Only staff with a valid TR (agent) licence for a line of business should be able to open a sales journey for that line. Tie permissions to the register, not to job titles.
**Audit trail for approvals:** Keep the responsible officer's approval record, with its date and conditions under s.64ZG, so that the bank can show who was approved and when.
bankNotes: **Authorized institution:** A bank carrying on insurance intermediary business is an authorized institution, as defined in Cap. 41 s.2 by reference to BO s.2(1). The insurance licence is granted under Cap. 41 in addition to the banking authorization.

**HKMA supervision:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority, a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases). The IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)), and must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)).

**Separate registers:** Bank staff who sell insurance need TR licences under Cap. 41 (s.64G(1), (3)(c)), whatever their HKMA register entries. The HKMA's IB-1 module was reportedly revised in November 2025; confirm the current text with the HKMA.

**Winding-up carve-out:** Section 76 bars the IA from petitioning to wind up a licensed intermediary that is an authorized institution. Failure of the bank's intermediary business is therefore not handled by that route. Check the position with the HKMA before drafting any contingency plan.
pitfalls: **Filing before the insurer appointment:** An agency application without an insurer appointment fails s.64U(5)(b). Sequence the appointment and the filing.
**Losing the only responsible officer:** Suspension can follow under s.64ZN(1), and revocation after 90 days under s.64ZN(2). A back-up officer avoids the cliff.
**Late notices:** Missing the 14-day notice periods in ss.64Q, 64R and 64P is an offence in each case. Late notices are easy to miss when sales teams change quickly.
**Assuming HKMA registration covers insurance:** A securities or banking register entry does not replace a TR (agent) licence under Cap. 41. Confirm each seller's status on the IA register.

**Unlicensed referrals:** An insurer must not accept a referral from a person in Hong Kong unless that person is licensed, or has only clerical duties (s.64N(2)). Plan referral journeys with that test in mind.

glossary.definition: An individual approved by the IA, who must be a licensed TR (agent) or applicant for one, and who helps the agency maintain conduct controls (ss.64ZE, 91).
An individual licensed to carry on regulated activities as agent of one licensed insurance agency (s.64Y).
A sole proprietor, partnership or company holding an agency licence to act as agent of one or more authorized insurers (s.64U).
An insurer authorized under Cap. 41 to carry on insurance business, which can appoint agencies and individual agents.
A bank or other institution authorized under the Banking Ordinance (Cap. 155). Cap. 41 s.2(1) adopts the Banking Ordinance meaning.
The IA's standard for licensing and officer approval, weighing competence, honesty, reputation, financial standing and disciplinary history (s.64ZZA).
A person who holds at least 15% of capital, profits or votes, or who exercises ultimate control over management (s.64F).
The head of the HKMA, to whom the IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business (s.4G).
The Insurance Intermediaries Qualifying Examination, run under the IIQAS scheme, which the IA's application notes link to individual licensing.

title: Conduct: best interests, needs analysis & disclosure
oneLiner: Every sale is governed by statutory conduct duties, which the codes, IA guidelines and the bank's own sales policy then make concrete.
keyPoints: **Statute first:** Section 90 sets nine conduct duties for every licensed insurance intermediary carrying on a regulated activity, from honesty and best interests to client assets.
**Firms carry controls:** Sections 91 and 92 require agencies and broker companies to maintain controls, use best endeavours and give their responsible officer real authority and resources.
**Breach is not automatically a lawsuit:** Section 93 says a failure to comply does not by itself create judicial liability. It does not stop IA discipline.
**Discipline route:** Section 80 defines [[misconduct]] to include contravening the Ordinance, and s.81 lets the IA act against regulated persons who are guilty of it.
**Codes and guidelines:** Section 95 codes and s.133 guidelines supply the detail. Neither is subsidiary legislation, but both are admissible in court.
**Counsel's role:** Turn each duty into a control, a sales step and a record the bank can produce on request.

conceptMap.caption: How the conduct duties reach a customer in the app.

items.label: Statute s.90
items.note: Nine duties for intermediaries

deepDive.heading: The statutory conduct duties
deepDive.lede: Section 90 sets the core duties every licensed insurance intermediary owes when carrying on a regulated activity.

visual.caption: The s.90 duties, grouped by what they protect.

items.label: Honesty and best interests
items.note: Act honestly, fairly and with integrity

items.label: Care, skill and competence
items.note: Advise only where competent

items.label: Regard to circumstances
items.note: The sale must suit the customer

items.label: Material disclosure
items.note: Enough information for material decisions

items.label: Conflicts
items.note: Best endeavours to avoid, and disclose

items.label: Client assets
items.note: Promptly and properly accounted for

items.label: Prescribed rules
items.note: Other rules made under ss.94 and 129

points: **Scope:** The duties apply when the intermediary carries on a regulated activity, so the bank's route and the product type both matter (see stage 2).
**Best interests:** Section 90(a) requires the intermediary to act in the best interests of the policy holder or potential policy holder. It is a statutory duty, not only a code principle.

**Customer facts:** Section 90(d) requires regard to the customer's particular circumstances. Section 90(e) requires enough disclosure for the customer to be sufficiently informed for any material decision.
**Competence:** Section 90(c) allows advice only on matters the intermediary is competent to advise on. This matters for any in-app guidance that goes beyond product facts.
**Conflicts:** Section 90(f) requires best endeavours to avoid a conflict with the customer. Section 90(g) requires disclosure of any conflict mentioned in paragraph (f).
deepDive.takeaway: Map each sales step to one s.90 duty, and keep evidence that the step was completed.

deepDive.heading: Firm-level duties: agencies and broker companies
deepDive.lede: The firm must build the controls that secure compliance with section 90, not only the individual adviser.
points: **Agencies (s.91):** A licensed insurance agency must establish and maintain proper controls, and use best endeavours to secure observance by its licensed technical representatives (agent).
**Broker companies (s.92):** A licensed insurance broker company carries the same control duties for its licensed technical representatives (broker).

**Responsible officer:** The responsible officer must use best endeavours to ensure the firm has those controls. The firm must give that officer sufficient authority, resources and support (s.91(1)(c)-(d), (2); s.92 is to the same effect).
**Route matters:** Which section applies depends on whether the bank sells through an agency or a broker company. Confirm the route in stage 3.

**Management:** Under s.80(3)-(4), conduct by an agency can also count as misconduct by a responsible officer or a person concerned in its management, where it arose from their consent, connivance or neglect.
deepDive.takeaway: Put the controls in writing and name the responsible officer before the app goes live.

deepDive.heading: Codes of conduct and guidelines
deepDive.lede: The codes and guidelines turn the statutory principles into practice expectations that the IA can weigh.

visual.caption: The two codes under s.95 cover the two intermediary types (reported).

items.label: Agents' Code
items.note: For licensed insurance agents, effective 23 Sep 2019 (reported)

items.label: Brokers' Code
items.note: For licensed insurance brokers, effective 23 Sep 2019 (reported)

points: **What they are:** Under s.95 the IA may publish codes giving guidance on practices and standards that licensed intermediaries are ordinarily expected to follow.

**Legal weight:** A breach does not by itself create liability (s.95(5)). A court must still take relevant provisions into account, and the IA may weigh a breach in a fit-and-proper assessment (s.95(6)-(7)).
**Guidelines:** Under s.133 the IA may publish guidelines on its functions or on how a provision works. They carry the same no-liability and admissibility structure (s.133(4)-(5)).
**Continuing training:** Section 95(3)(b) allows a code to require continuous training, so the conduct duties can run beyond the point of sale.
**Check the wording:** The codes' wording on best interests, needs analysis and suitability should be checked in the current text. Read both codes before drafting policy text.
deepDive.takeaway: Build the sales policy from the codes and guidelines, and map each clause to an app control.

deepDive.heading: Needs analysis and suitability
deepDive.lede: Before recommending certain policies, the intermediary must understand the customer's needs and ability to pay.
points: **Statutory base:** Section 90(d) requires regard to the customer's circumstances. GL30 on financial needs analysis (FNA) is the IA's detailed guidance on how to do that for covered policies.

**Product scope:** An FNA is required before recommending a policy under GL30. An industry FNA initiative (2018) is reported to limit scope to Class A and C policies, with exclusions. Confirm the scope in GL30 itself.
**What an FNA covers:** Reported inputs are the customer's needs, financial situation and ability to pay premiums. Check the steps in GL30 in the current text.
**Competence:** Section 90(c) allows advice only on matters the intermediary is competent to advise on. This matters for any in-app guidance that goes beyond product facts.
**Investment-linked products:** Investment-linked products raise a separate risk-profiling and suitability question, covered in stage 8. Check the detailed rules before relying on them.
**Records:** Keep the needs analysis with the application, so the bank can show what the customer said and why the product fitted.
deepDive.takeaway: Treat the FNA as a gate: no recommendation in the app until the record is complete.

deepDive.heading: Disclosure, capacity and cooling-off
deepDive.lede: Disclosure rules tell the customer who the intermediary acts for, what it earns, and how to cancel before the customer commits.
points: **Capacity:** The customer must know whether the intermediary acts as an insurer's agent or as a broker. Section 90(e) requires the disclosure needed for material decisions; check the codes' exact capacity wording in the current text.
**Conflicts:** Under s.90(g), any conflict the intermediary cannot avoid must be disclosed. Remuneration and group links are the usual sources of conflict.

**Remuneration:** For ILAS sold by banks, an HKMA circular of 22 April 2013 is reported to require written pre-sale disclosure of the monetary and non-monetary benefits the bank receives. Confirm the current text.
**Benefit illustrations:** GL28 governs illustrations for long-term policies. Check its current text before the app shows projected values.

**Cooling-off:** IA guideline GL29 gives a cooling-off period of 21 calendar days, from delivery of the policy or a Cooling-off Notice, whichever is earlier, for certain types of life insurance policies (its para 4.2 lists them; check the current text). It is a guideline under s.133, not law in itself.

**Gifts, rebates and replacement:** GL25 limits gifts for Class C products and sets conditions for long-term premium rebates. GL27 covers long-term policy replacement; check its current text before drafting replacement steps.
deepDive.takeaway: Put capacity, remuneration and the cancellation right on the first screens, not only in the terms.

deepDive.heading: Fair treatment and vulnerable customers
deepDive.lede: The Ordinance and the sources read do not set specific rules for vulnerable customers, so the bank must set and evidence its own standard.
points: **Baseline:** Sections 90(a) (fairly) and 90(b) (care and skill) apply to every customer, including elderly or vulnerable customers.
**Open point:** Specific IA rules on elderly customers, pre-sale calls and post-sale calls should be checked in the current text. Do not assume a call requirement exists.
**Complaints:** Complaint handling under the codes and the Ordinance is covered in stage 12.
**Design choice:** Plain language, more time to decide, and an option to speak to a person reduce risk. Check the current text for any required standard.
deepDive.takeaway: Write a vulnerable-customer standard and test it in the journey before launch.

provisions.title: Conduct requirements for licensed insurance intermediaries
provisions.summary: Requires a licensed insurance intermediary carrying on a regulated activity to meet nine duties: honesty and fairness, best interests, care and skill, competence, regard to circumstances, material disclosure, conflict avoidance and disclosure, client assets, and prescribed rules.
provisions.counselNote: Trace every sales step to one of these duties. Section 90(a) on best interests is the anchor for the whole sales policy.

provisions.title: Conduct requirements for licensed insurance agencies and their responsible officers
provisions.summary: A licensed insurance agency must maintain controls that secure s.90 compliance by itself and its licensed technical representatives (agent), and use best endeavours to secure observance. It must also give its responsible officer authority, resources and support.
provisions.counselNote: If the bank sells through an agency, check that the agency's responsible officer has the authority and resources the section requires.

provisions.title: Conduct requirements for licensed insurance broker companies and their responsible officers
provisions.summary: Imposes the same control, best-endeavours and responsible-officer duties on a licensed insurance broker company, in respect of its licensed technical representatives (broker).
provisions.counselNote: Relevant if the bank works with a broker company rather than an agency. Confirm the route in stage 3.

provisions.title: Breach of conduct requirements
provisions.summary: A failure to comply with s.90, 91 or 92 does not by itself make any person liable to judicial proceedings. Other liability, including under the common law, is unaffected.
provisions.counselNote: This is not a safe harbour. A breach can still be misconduct under s.80, leading to IA discipline under s.81, and common-law claims remain possible.

provisions.title: Interpretation
provisions.summary: Defines misconduct to include contravening the Ordinance, a licence term or condition, and an act or omission that the IA considers prejudicial to policy holders or the public interest. For the last limb the IA must have regard to codes and guidelines in force.
provisions.counselNote: Codes and guidelines shape what counts as prejudicial conduct, so their current text drives discipline risk.

provisions.title: Disciplinary action in respect of regulated persons
provisions.summary: Allows the IA to take disciplinary action against a regulated person who is or was guilty of misconduct, or who is not a fit and proper person.
provisions.counselNote: Discipline can reach the responsible officer and persons concerned in management, not only the firm. Plan the response with each of them in mind.

provisions.title: Codes of conduct for licensed insurance intermediaries
provisions.summary: The IA may publish codes of conduct on practices and standards for licensed intermediaries. A breach does not by itself create liability, but a code may be weighed in fit-and-proper decisions and is admissible in court. A code may require continuous training.
provisions.counselNote: The current Agents' and Brokers' Codes are the detailed conduct benchmark. Track amendments, which the IA may make under s.95(4).

provisions.title: Codes or guidelines on functions of Authority, etc.
provisions.summary: The IA may publish guidelines on its functions or on how a provision operates. A breach does not by itself create liability, but guidelines are admissible in court and must be considered where relevant.
provisions.counselNote: This is the general power for IA guidelines. It is reported as the basis for GL24 and GL25; check the current text for the statutory basis of GL29 and GL30 before citing it.

provisions.instrument: Code of Conduct for Licensed Insurance Agents (issued under s.95)
provisions.title: Code of Conduct for Licensed Insurance Agents
provisions.summary: Sets out fundamental principles of professional conduct for licensed insurance agents, covering conduct toward clients, disclosure and conflicts (reported; check the current text). Effective 23 September 2019 (reported).
provisions.counselNote: Governs the bank's agency channel, if used. Read the principles in the official text. Check the current text for themes such as best interests.

provisions.instrument: Code of Conduct for Licensed Insurance Brokers (issued under s.95)
provisions.title: Code of Conduct for Licensed Insurance Brokers
provisions.summary: The companion code for licensed insurance brokers, effective 23 September 2019 (reported). It applies to the broker route in the way the agents' code applies to the agency route.
provisions.counselNote: Relevant if the bank uses a broker route. Compare its principles with the agents' code before settling the partner model.

provisions.instrument: IA Guideline on Financial Needs Analysis (GL30)
provisions.title: Financial needs analysis
provisions.summary: Requires a financial needs analysis before recommending certain life insurance policies (reported). Interpretation Notes (version 8, 26 August 2020) explain the requirements. Check the product scope and steps in the official text.
provisions.counselNote: Confirm the covered products before designing the FNA gate. Build the FNA as mandatory for those products until the full guideline has been checked.

provisions.title: Cooling-off period
provisions.summary: Gives a policy holder 21 calendar days from delivery of the policy or a Cooling-off Notice, whichever is earlier, to cancel and receive a premium refund, for certain types of life insurance policies (para 4.2). Applies to authorized insurers and licensed intermediaries.
provisions.counselNote: Build the cancellation option and refund into the post-sale flow. Some products are reported to carry 30 days. Check each product.

checklist: Map each s.90(a)-(i) duty to a control, a sales step and an evidence record.
Confirm whether the bank sells through a licensed agency (s.91) or a broker company (s.92), and who the responsible officer is.
Pull the current Agents' and Brokers' Codes and check every clause against the app journey.
Confirm which products trigger a GL30 financial needs analysis, and build the FNA as a gate before recommendation.
Check the GL29 cooling-off rule for each product, including any longer period.
Confirm the GL28 benefit illustration rules before showing projected values in the app.
Show capacity, remuneration and conflicts before the customer decides, and test that the customer sees them.
Adopt a written policy on gifts, rebates and inducements, checked against GL25.
itAngle: **Journey logic:** Conduct duties depend on sequence. Build the needs questions, disclosures and cooling-off notice as fixed steps the customer cannot skip.
**Data for the FNA:** The needs analysis may use data the bank already holds. Use it with consent and record where each input came from.
**Records:** Store the FNA, disclosure acknowledgements and advice records in a form that is retrievable for complaints and IA inspection.
**Testing:** Test for skipped steps, back-button loops and failed submissions. A gap in the flow is a conduct failure, not only a bug.
bankNotes: **Bank as intermediary:** If the bank sells through a licensed agency or broker company, ss.90-92 bind that firm, so the bank's own controls must match the firm's.
**HKMA interest:** The HKMA expects banks to apply its investor-protection measures to insurance sales where relevant. This is reported guidance; confirm the HKMA source before relying on it.
**Staff incentives:** Bank staff incentive schemes tied to insurance sales raise conflict and inducement questions under s.90(f)-(g) and the codes.
**Premium financing:** Where the bank also lends for premium financing, HKMA circulars from 1 April 2022 address banks acting as both intermediary and financier (check the current text).
**Overlap with SFC:** Investment-linked sales overlap with SFC suitability expectations for investment products. Confirm the split with stage 8.
pitfalls: **Reading s.93 as a safe harbour:** Section 93(1) means a breach does not by itself create judicial liability. Section 93(2) preserves common-law liability, and misconduct under s.80 can still lead to IA discipline under s.81.
**Quoting code wording from memory:** Quote only wording checked against the official edition, since the IA may amend codes under s.95(4).
**Ignoring remote selling:** Remote sales change how disclosure and cooling-off steps are shown. Check the remote-selling rules in stage 9.
**Using a gift or rebate as a sales hook:** Promotions can breach GL25. Route each offer through compliance before launch.

glossary.definition: A person licensed under Cap. 41 to carry on regulated activities, such as a licensed insurance agency or broker company. Section 90 applies to licensed insurance intermediaries.

An act listed in Sch. 1A, Pt 1 (s.3A(a)): negotiating or arranging a contract of insurance, inviting or inducing a person to enter one or to make a material decision, or giving regulated advice. The s.90 duties depend on it.
The statutory standard in s.90(a) that the intermediary act in the policy holder's best interests, not only the interests of the bank or the insurer.
Defined in s.80(1) to include contravening the Ordinance, a licence term, or an act or omission the IA considers prejudicial to policy holders or the public interest. It is the ground for discipline.
An individual approved by the IA to act as the firm's responsible officer. Under ss.91(2) and 92(2) the officer must use best endeavours to secure the firm's controls.
A situation where the intermediary's interests and the customer's may diverge. Section 90(f) requires best endeavours to avoid it, and s.90(g) requires disclosure.
The IA's structured assessment of a customer's needs, finances and ability to pay before a recommendation, set out in GL30 for covered products.
A window in which the policy holder may cancel and receive a premium refund. IA guideline GL29 sets 21 calendar days for certain types of life insurance policies.
Guidance the IA publishes under s.95 on practices and standards for licensed intermediaries. It is not subsidiary legislation, but it is admissible in court.

title: Savings, investment-linked & participating policies
oneLiner: Higher-risk long term products need two regulators, stronger disclosure and the bank's own controls on top of the usual sales rules.
keyPoints: **Scope:** Savings, investment-linked ([[ILAS]]) and participating policies are long term business under Part IV of Cap. 41. The customer often bears investment or bonus risk that a plain protection policy does not carry.
**ILAS:** An investment-linked assurance scheme is linked long term business (class C). It is also a collective investment scheme that the SFC must authorize before it is offered to the public.
**Participating policies:** Bonuses are declared, not guaranteed. Benefit illustrations and the fulfilment ratio shape how the customer judges value, so both need careful control.
**Tax-linked annuities:** A deferred annuity premium is deductible only if the IA certifies the policy and the customer meets the tax conditions.
**Premium financing:** A loan that pays the premium adds credit risk. A bank that both lends and sells creates a conflict that must be avoided or disclosed.
**Counsel's role:** Confirm which regulator approves each product, which disclosures apply, and what evidence the bank's sales journey must produce.

points: **Class C (linked):** Sch. 1, Pt 2 covers life and annuity contracts whose benefits are wholly or partly linked to investments. Class C is the core ILAS classification.
**Separate funds:** s.21B(2)(a) requires an authorized insurer to keep a separate account and fund for class C business. Classes G and H are treated the same way under s.21B(2)(b) and (c).
**Participating sub-fund:** s.21B(3) requires at least one separate sub-fund for participating business within the specified business fund.
**Universal life:** Classify first. A secondary source reports that indexed universal life falls under class C; confirm this against the product terms and the IA text.
**Product choice:** A bank's product list should show the class of each product, because the class determines the approval and fund rules that apply.
deepDive.takeaway: Classify every product before any other regulatory step.

deepDive.heading: ILAS: two approvals and two regulators
deepDive.lede: An ILAS needs SFC authorization of the scheme and of its offering documents, and the IA regulates the insurance sale.

items.note: Advertisements and documents need SFC authorization

points: **Scheme approval:** SFO s.104(1) lets the SFC authorize a collective investment scheme, subject to conditions. Under s.104(2), an approved person must be in place to receive the SFC's notices.
**Offering documents:** SFO s.105(1) lets the SFC authorize any advertisement, invitation or document that invites an act described in s.103(1)(a) or (b). App copy and brochures fall within this.
**Offence risk:** An SFC FAQ summary reports that issuing an ILAS to the public without authorization is an offence under s.103. Professional investors are not caught (SFO s.103(2)(k)).
**Securities reading:** On the text of SFO Sch. 1, an insurance-wrapped ILAS may fall outside "securities". This is counsel's reading, not a settled SFC position, so confirm it before launch.
**Other products:** Selling funds or bonds alongside an ILAS can trigger a securities licence requirement. Keep the app's product scope clear.
deepDive.takeaway: Obtain the SFC authorizations first, then build the sales flow around them.

deepDive.heading: Participating policies
deepDive.lede: Participating bonuses are not guaranteed, so the customer relies on illustrations and the insurer's track record.
points: **Non-guaranteed benefits:** Part of the illustrated benefit depends on bonuses the insurer declares later. The customer may receive less than the illustration shows.

**Benefit illustrations:** GL28 governs benefit illustrations for long term policies. A 2025 IA practice note on illustration rate caps supplements it, and a secondary source reports that the caps took effect on 1 July 2025.

**Fulfilment ratio:** This measures how far declared bonuses match the amounts illustrated at sale, by product series. Obtain the insurer's calculation method and the IA material it relies on, and confirm it before use.

**Revised GL16:** The IA is reported to have revised GL16 (underwriting long term business other than class C) on 6 February 2026, effective 31 March 2026 (reported; check the IA text). Confirm commencement before relying on any disclosure duty.
**Customer expectations:** Check the IA's current position on how far customers may rely on non-guaranteed bonuses before describing them.

**Asset ring-fence:** Under s.23(1), assets of a fund kept for part of the business may only be applied for that part of the business. Blurring participating assets with the bank's own funds is a risk to avoid.
deepDive.takeaway: Test every projection against the fulfilment ratio history before the customer sees it.

deepDive.heading: Annuities and tax-linked products
deepDive.lede: Tax-linked products work only where the IA certifies the policy and the customer meets the tax rules.
points: **QDAP basis:** The Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), ss.26N to 26U, allows a deduction for premiums on certified deferred annuity policies. This is reported and should be checked against the current statute text before use.

**Certification:** The IA certifies policies that meet its guideline GL19, which is reported as issued under s.133 of Cap. 41. Certification is not an endorsement and does not guarantee the customer's deduction.
**Cap:** The IA's QDAP page gives an annual limit of HK$60,000. The page notes that this is shared with certain MPF voluntary contributions. Confirm the current figure before quoting it.
**Timing:** Only premiums due and paid in a year of assessment count toward that year's deduction.
**VHIS:** Certified health plans are certified by the Health Bureau, not the IA. Stage 4 covers the sales rules for them.
deepDive.takeaway: Build the QDAP journey around certification and the customer's own tax position.

deepDive.heading: Premium financing
deepDive.lede: Lending to buy a policy adds credit risk, and a bank that both lends and sells has a built-in conflict.
points: **Who is bound:** Section 90 binds a licensed insurance intermediary when it carries on a regulated activity. A bank licensed as an intermediary is bound directly. A bank selling through a licensed agency should expect that agency to owe these duties, and should test its own controls against them.

**HKMA press release of 1 April 2022:** This announces an HKMA circular that addresses banks acting as both insurance intermediary and premium financing provider, after a 2020 joint inspection with the IA.

**Later circulars:** Reported HKMA circulars of 16 October 2023 and 19 November 2025 cover the interest-rate basis for premium financing and the separation of financing from the insurance application. Check the originals.
**Promotions:** The 2025 review is reported to prohibit return-enhancing promotions tied to premium financing.
**Recent item:** A reported HKMA letter of August 2026 forwards an IA circular dated 20 August 2026 on premium financing for long term policies. Its status and content need checking before launch.
deepDive.takeaway: Keep the loan decision and the insurance application in separate journeys, with clear disclosure of the bank's interest in both.

deepDive.heading: Customers and controls
deepDive.lede: Higher-risk products need stronger suitability checks, plain exit disclosures and follow-up.
points: **Risk profiling:** Use a financial needs analysis under GL30 and a risk profile before recommending a linked or participating product. The HKMA's 2022 guidance on protection linked plans refers to these tools.
**Concentration:** Limit premium financing and single-product concentration for each customer. Flag repeat purchases for review.
**Older customers:** Check age, income and retirement horizon. If no HKMA circular on vulnerable customers applies, the bank should set its own test.
**Exit terms:** Explain surrender values, early termination charges and any loss of capital in plain language, at the point of sale.

**Post-sale follow-up:** Use confirmation calls or digital checks after sale. Separately, the HKMA's December 2024 circular allows alternative digital measures in place of audio recording at sale, subject to conditions. It excludes protection linked plans.
deepDive.takeaway: The needs analysis, the disclosure and the sale should all point to the same product.

checklist: Confirm the SFC authorization status of each ILAS (s.104 scheme, s.105 documents) before any app copy goes live.
Classify each product as class C, participating, annuity or other, and map it to the correct fund and disclosure rules.
Discuss any ILAS or PLP launch with the HKMA beforehand, as the 8 July 2022 and 30 August 2023 HKMA circulars are reported to expect (reported; check both circulars), and record the date.
Check the current GL28 text and rate caps before publishing any benefit illustration.
Show the fulfilment ratio history for each participating series in the sales journey, where the insurer discloses it.
Separate the premium financing journey from the insurance application, and log each s.90(g) conflict disclosure.
Confirm QDAP certification, the deduction cap and the year-of-assessment rules against the IA and IRD sources.
Set a vulnerable-customer and concentration test for the bank's own long term products, since the HKMA's current position on vulnerable customers should be checked.
itAngle: **Product catalogue:** Tag every product with its class, SFC status, IA certification and fund type. Filter the app by these tags, not by marketing name.
**Illustration engine:** Projections for participating and ILAS products must follow the guideline assumptions. Version each illustration so it shows its assumptions and date.
**Fulfilment data feed:** Ingest the insurer's fulfilment ratio history and display it next to the illustration. Refresh it on each disclosure cycle.
**Separate journeys:** Build the premium financing and the insurance application as separate flows, with separate consents and audit logs.
bankNotes: **Bank as lender and seller:** A bank that lends to buy a policy and then sells the policy has a built-in conflict. s.90(f) and (g) are the anchors, and HKMA circulars test how the bank manages it.

**HKMA prior notice:** HKMA circulars on selling protection linked plans (8 July 2022 and 30 August 2023) are reported to expect a bank to discuss an ILAS launch with the HKMA beforehand (reported; check both circulars).

**Investment corner and recording:** Secondary sources report HKMA circulars of 2011 and 2013 on investment corners and pre-sale disclosure for ILAS. Later circulars of 2019 and December 2024 set recording rules. Check each current version.
**Bank-linked agency:** If the bank sells through its own appointed agency, that agency must be licensed. The bank's controls should match the duties the licensed firm owes under s.90.

**HKMA delegation:** The IA has delegated its inspection and investigation powers over authorized institutions' insurance business to the Monetary Authority (HKMA), a delegation in place since 23 September 2019 (s.4G; reported in IA and HKMA releases), and the IA can still act itself (s.4G(5)). The IA must consult the Monetary Authority before investigating or disciplining a bank (ss.64ZZH(2), 82(4), 84(4)).
pitfalls: **Treating ILAS as an ordinary fund:** An ILAS is both a Cap. 41 product and an SFC-authorized scheme. Skipping either approval creates offence risk under SFO s.103, per an SFC FAQ summary.
**Using the highest illustration:** A projection that assumes the top bonus rate misleads the customer. Use approved assumptions and state that bonuses are not guaranteed.
**Assuming the QDAP deduction:** Certification does not guarantee the customer's deduction, which depends on the customer's own tax position.
**Treating 2026 items as settled:** The August 2026 HKMA letter, the 20 August 2026 IA circular and the revised GL16 are reported; check the current texts before relying on them.

A long term policy with flexible premiums and an account value, often linked to an index or investments. Its class depends on its terms.
A contract that pays regular income for a set period, usually from a chosen age or date.

title: Digital sales, data & outsourcing
oneLiner: Selling insurance in an app changes the channel, not the law. Consent, records, algorithms and cyber controls all need an owner.
keyPoints: **Same duties, new channel:** The app does not change the conduct rules. Section 90 binds any licensed intermediary carrying on a regulated activity. Section 91 adds controls and duties for the licensed agency and its responsible officer.
**Advice by algorithm:** Automated needs analysis is still advice by the licensed intermediary. Responsibility stays with the agency and its [[Responsible officer]]. Software cannot take it over.

**Electronic contracts:** Where a rule of law requires a signature, the Electronic Transactions Ordinance accepts an e-signature that is reliable, appropriate and consented to by the other party (s.6(1)). IA guidance on internet insurance activities (GL8), reported to apply to these sales, should be read in full before design freeze.
**Personal data:** Collection notices, purpose limits and consent for [[Direct marketing]] under PDPO Part 6A apply to every data flow, including sharing with the insurer partner.
**Records and inspection:** The IA can inspect and copy business records, including records held in information systems. Each journey version must be retrievable.
**Counsel's role:** Map each app step to a legal duty, a control and an owner, then fix the split of duties with the insurer before launch.

deepDive.heading: Online and remote sales
deepDive.lede: Selling in an app is still a sale. The IA guidance and the e-signature rules decide what the app must do.
points: **Distribution route:** An authorized insurer must not contract through another person unless that person is a licensed insurance agency or licensed individual insurance agent appointed by the insurer, a licensed insurance broker company, or only does clerical or administrative duties (s.64N(1)(a), (b)).

**Internet guidance:** The IA's Guideline on the Use of Internet for Insurance Activities (GL8) is reported to cover insurers, intermediaries and other groups doing insurance business wholly or partly online. [Reported; read the full text.]
**Accurate materials:** GL8 is reported to require online sales materials and illustrations to be accurate and kept up to date.

**Remote video sales:** The IA's circular of 5 August 2020 set terms for video-conference sales of long-term policies under the InsurTech sandbox. The HKMA's December 2024 circular added audio alternatives for video sales of investment and annuity products. Check the current IA status.

**Electronic signatures:** Where a rule of law requires a signature, ETO s.6(1) accepts an electronic signature if the method is reliable and appropriate and the other party consents (s.6(1)(c) to (e)). The section does not apply where a government entity is a party (s.6(1)(b)). Schedule 1 excludes wills, trusts, powers of attorney and some other documents, but not insurance contracts.
deepDive.takeaway: Map every online step to a consent, a signature method and a record of what the customer saw.

deepDive.heading: Advice by algorithm and generated content
deepDive.lede: Automated advice is still regulated advice. The licensed person stays responsible for it.
points: **Same duties:** Section 90 applies to a licensed intermediary carrying on a regulated activity. It requires honest, fair conduct in the best interests of the customer, and regard to the customer's circumstances (s.90(a), (d)).
**Codes of conduct:** Section 90 is read with the codes of conduct made under s.95. Check the current code for any rule on electronic sales before design.

**Responsibility:** The agency must maintain controls for itself and its licensed technical representatives (s.91(1)(a)). Its responsible officer must use best endeavours to ensure those controls exist and are observed (s.91(2)).
**Narrow public advice exception:** Section 123(1)(f)(iii) stops s.64G from prohibiting regulated advice given through electronic communication to the public. It covers advice only.

**Inviting and arranging remain regulated:** The exception does not reach inviting or inducing a person to buy (Sch. 1A, Pt 1, item 1(b)) or negotiating or arranging a contract (item 1(a)). A flow from advice to purchase still needs a licensed route.
**Testing and records:** Test the logic, versions and outputs of the engine, and keep them. Records held in information systems must be producible in legible form (s.64ZZS).
deepDive.takeaway: Treat the algorithm as a tool of the licensed person, and document its design, testing and changes.

deepDive.heading: Personal data
deepDive.lede: The app collects more data than a branch does, and each use needs its own legal basis under the PDPO.
points: **Collection notice:** Data protection principle 1 requires data to be collected for a lawful purpose, adequate but not excessive, and the customer must be told whether supply is obligatory and what follows if not (PDPO Sch. 1, DPP1).

**Direct marketing:** Part 6A governs use of data in direct marketing (ss.35A-35M). Section 35C requires specified steps first, and s.35E(1) bars use without consent that matches the kind of data and the class of marketing subjects.

**Cross-selling:** Offering insurance from the bank's own customer data is direct marketing. A breach of s.35E(1) is an offence carrying a fine of $500,000 and 3 years' imprisonment on conviction (s.35E(4)).

**Sharing with the insurer:** Providing data to an insurer for its own marketing needs the customer's written consent, covering the permitted kind of data and the permitted class of recipients and marketing subjects. If the data is provided for gain, the notice must say so (s.35K(1), (2)).

**Cross-border transfer:** Section 33 would restrict transfers outside Hong Kong. It is reported as not yet in force, so check its commencement on eLegislation and with the PCPD before relying on it either way. The six data protection principles apply regardless.
deepDive.takeaway: Build separate consents for the bank's marketing and the insurer's marketing, and keep the proof of each.

deepDive.heading: Cybersecurity and outsourcing
deepDive.lede: The insurer and the bank each carry cyber duties, and the insurance journey runs across both systems.
points: **Insurer duties:** The IA's Guideline on Cybersecurity (GL20), issued under s.133(1), was revised with effect from 1 January 2025 (reported; check the current text). It applies to authorized insurers. It is reported to require notice of reportable incidents to the IA within 72 hours of detection.
**Scope gap:** Check whether GL20 binds licensed intermediaries directly. Confirm the bank's own duties before assuming the insurer's controls cover the app.

**Bank's framework:** The bank already works under HKMA technology risk and outsourcing requirements. Map the insurance journey and each insurer interface into them rather than building a parallel regime.
**Interfaces:** Each quote or policy API needs an agreed data map, access controls and logging. The insurer and the bank should each own the controls on their side.
**Incident clocks:** Notify each regulator under its own rules and timing. Do not assume one clock covers both.
**HKMA side:** Identify the bank's own incident-notice expectation in the current HKMA supervisory module on cyber or technology risk, and check its timing against that module.
deepDive.takeaway: Agree in writing who owns each control and each notification clock before go-live.

deepDive.heading: Records and evidence
deepDive.lede: Regulators judge a sale by its record. Keep what the customer saw, agreed and signed.
points: **Inspection powers:** An IA inspector may enter business premises, inspect and copy business records, and require answers about them (s.64ZZF(2), (3)). This applies to licensed insurance intermediaries.

**Information systems:** Where a record required under s.64ZZF or s.64ZZH is recorded in a form that is not legible, the IA may require a legible reproduction, including one from an information system (s.64ZZS). App logs and databases are within reach.
**What to keep:** Each journey version, the disclosures shown, consents, e-signature evidence and any calls or chats.

**Retention period:** AMLO Sch. 2, s.20 requires at least five years for CDD and transaction records of the agency's in-scope transactions (stage 10). Check whether the IA sets a general period for conduct records, and agree the bank's period with the insurer.
**Replay test:** Be able to reproduce the screen a customer saw on a given date. This is the practical test of s.64ZZS and of the ETO reliability test.
deepDive.takeaway: Build the evidence trail into the product, not into an after-the-fact file.
